sections.heading: 1. The Call to Adventure
sections.title: The Call to Adventure
sections.text:
The fluorescent lights of your office flicker above you, a constant 
reminder that you’re still here, trapped in the same lifeless 
cubicle, scrolling through social media while your boss thinks 
you're working on a quarterly report. Another entrepreneur just 
posted about making six figures in their sleep. Someone else 
launched a simple product that went viral overnight. And here you 
are, sipping cold coffee and wondering if there’s more to life than 
emails marked "urgent" that somehow never seem that urgent. 
Then, it hits you. You could do this too. You’ve got ideas. 
Maybe even a great one. What’s stopping you from launching 
your own business and taking control of your future? You sit up 
straighter, adrenaline buzzing through your veins. It’s time to 
make a move. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Quit your job immediately and go all in! → Go to 2 
●​ Side hustle while keeping your job. → Go to 3 
●​ Buy a “Get Rich Quick” course from a guru. → Go to 4

sections.heading: 2. The Leap of Faith
sections.title: The Leap of Faith
sections.text:
You close your eyes, take a deep breath, and before you can talk 
yourself out of it, you do it. You draft the resignation email, hit 
send, and lean back in your chair. A wave of adrenaline rushes 
through you. No more bosses. No more meetings. No more 
wasted time. 
By the time you walk out of the office for the last time, reality 
starts creeping in. No more steady paycheck, either. You have 
savings, but it won’t last forever. Now, the clock is ticking. 
Back home, you sit in front of your laptop, staring at a blank 
screen. What’s your next move? 
●​ Start building a website and brand identity right away. 
→ Go to 5 
●​ Figure out who your audience is and what they 
actually need. → Go to 6 
●​ Go straight into selling something, figure out the 
details later. → Go to 7

sections.heading: 3. The Cautious Climb
sections.title: The Cautious Climb
sections.text:
You decide to play it safe. You’re not ready to give up the comfort 
of a steady paycheck just yet. Instead, you commit to working on 
your business during evenings and weekends. It’s going to be 
exhausting, but at least you won’t be homeless if things don’t 
work out. 
Each night after work, you pour over YouTube tutorials, marketing 
blogs, and startup success stories. You start making slow 
progress, sketching out your ideas and mapping out a plan. But 
balancing work and a side hustle isn’t easy. Your boss is starting 
to notice your decreased enthusiasm at work, and your social 
life? Well, let’s just say your favorite streaming service has 
started asking if you’re still alive. 
What’s your next step? 
●​ Focus on learning and planning before taking any big 
risks. → Go to 8 
●​ Test the waters by offering a service or selling a small 
product. → Go to 9 
●​ Take out a small loan to speed up the process. → Go 
to 10

sections.heading: 4. The Shortcut Gamble
sections.title: The Shortcut Gamble
sections.text:
Scrolling through social media, you stumble across an ad that 
practically screams at you: “Make $10K a month with my secret 
business blueprint!” The guru in the video stands in front of a 
rented Lamborghini, flashing screenshots of massive earnings. It 
looks… suspiciously easy. But hey, what if it actually works? 
You hover over the Buy Now button. For just $997, you could 
unlock the “secrets” to wealth. But do you even have that kind of 
money to spare? 
If you don't have enough Capital, you hesitate, realizing that 
throwing money at a random guru might not be the smartest 
move. Instead, you decide to: 
●​ Search for free resources and build your business 
from the ground up. → Go to 11 
●​ Try to borrow money from friends or family to invest 
in the course anyway. → Go to 12 
Otherwise, you take a deep breath and click.. For just $997, you 
could unlock the “secrets” to wealth. You take a deep breath and 
click. 
The next morning, you eagerly log into the course. Module 1: 
Mindset Training. Okay. Module 2: Believe in Yourself. Hmm. 
By Module 5, you realize you’ve just paid for a glorified 
motivational speech. The “business model” is vague at best, and 
the real “secret” seems to be… selling the same course to others. 
You sit back, wondering if you’ve just been scammed. What do 
you do next? 
●​ Try to salvage something from the course and 
implement the advice. → Go to 13 
●​ Cut your losses and start researching real business 
strategies. → Go to 14 
●​ Double down and buy another advanced course from 
the same guru. → Go to 15

sections.heading: 5. Building Your Brand
sections.title: Building Your Brand
sections.text:
You fire up your laptop and start sketching out the look and feel of 
your business. A logo? Definitely. A website? Of course. A 
professional email address? Goodbye, Gmail, hello 
you@yourbrand.com. 
The hours fly by as you tweak colors, pick fonts, and write an 
“About” page that makes you sound like the next big thing. But 
branding alone won’t bring in customers. You need a solid plan. 
What’s your next step? 
●​ Start posting on social media to attract attention. → 
Go to 16 
●​ Reach out to potential customers directly. → Go to 17 
●​ Invest in paid ads to get your brand in front of people 
faster. → Go to 18

sections.heading: 6. Understanding Your Audience
sections.title: Understanding Your Audience
sections.text:
You lean back in your chair, realizing that before you even think 
about selling something, you need to understand who your 
customers are. It doesn’t matter if you have the best product in 
the world, if you don’t know who needs it, you’re just shouting into 
the void. 
You start researching. Who exactly are you serving? Are they 
busy professionals, fitness junkies, freelancers, or maybe 
small business owners? The more you define them, the clearer 
your path becomes. What problem are you solving? What 
makes your offer irresistible? 
You jot down details about your ideal customer. Their pain points, 
desires, habits. This is your marketing avatar, your guiding light 
for everything you build next. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Conduct a survey or interview potential customers to 
confirm your assumptions. → Go to 19 
●​ Start crafting an offer based on your research. → Go 
to 20 
●​ Skip the research and just start selling. → Go to 21

sections.heading: 7. Diving in Headfirst
sections.title: Diving in Headfirst
sections.text:
You decide that planning is overrated. You’re not going to waste 
time overanalyzing. Instead, you pick a product or service and 
start selling immediately. 
You set up a basic offer, no website, no branding, just a clear 
value proposition. Maybe it’s consulting, a simple digital product, 
or flipping items online. Whatever it is, you’re moving fast. 
Now comes the first big risk. Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Your offer is strong, and customers start buying! → 
Go to 22 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed results. Some interest, but no big wins yet. 
→ Go to 23 
●​ 7 or below → Crickets. Time for a pivot. → Go to 24

sections.heading: 8. Strategic Learning
sections.title: Strategic Learning
sections.text:
You decide to take your time, soaking up knowledge before 
making any major moves. You dive into books, podcasts, and 
YouTube videos on entrepreneurship. Each day, you pick up 
something new, how to craft an irresistible offer, the psychology 
behind pricing, and the importance of branding. You fill notebooks 
with ideas, sketch out potential business models, and build 
confidence in your expertise. 
But as time passes, frustration starts creeping in. You have all 
this knowledge, but no action. You realize that learning is only 
half the battle. You need to start implementing. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Test a small idea with minimal risk and investment. → 
Go to 25 
●​ Create a detailed business plan before making any 
moves. → Go to 26 
●​ Ask your mentor to guide you through the early 
stages. → Go to 27

sections.heading: 9. Testing the Waters
sections.title: Testing the Waters
sections.text:
Instead of overthinking things, you decide to launch something 
small. Maybe it’s a simple freelance service, a digital product, or 
even flipping items for a quick profit. You throw together a quick 
pitch and put it out there, waiting to see if anyone bites. 
Now comes the first real test of the market. Roll 2d6 + 
Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Success! You land a few customers and gain early 
traction. → Go to 28 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed results. Some interest, but nothing 
sustainable yet. → Go to 29 
●​ 7 or below → Crickets. Nobody seems interested. Time 
for a rethink. → Go to 30

sections.heading: 10. Borrowing to Invest
sections.title: Borrowing to Invest
sections.text:
You decide that playing it safe isn’t going to get you anywhere 
fast. A little extra cash could help you launch quicker, so you 
explore your options. You could get a small business loan, put 
expenses on a credit card, or even borrow from family and 
friends. It feels like a gamble, but without money, growth will be 
slow. 
Now comes the risk. Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → You secure the funding with favorable terms and 
low interest. → Go to 31 
●​ 8-10 → You get the money, but it comes with challenges, 
high interest, pressure to repay fast. → Go to 32 
●​ 7 or below → No one is willing to lend you money, and 
now you’re stuck. → Go to 33

sections.heading: 11. Free Resources and Hustling
sections.title: Free Resources and Hustling
sections.text:
You decide that rather than throwing money at a questionable 
guru, you’ll take the bootstrapped approach. You start diving 
deep into free resources, business podcasts, YouTube tutorials, 
and case studies. Instead of shortcuts, you learn real strategies 
from people who have actually built businesses. 
Slowly, a picture forms in your mind: You need a real strategy, 
not a “secret formula.” You start taking notes, planning your 
next steps, and focusing on action instead of passive learning. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Find an industry or niche that interests you and 
research pain points. → Go to 34 
●​ Create a simple product or service based on what 
you’ve learned. → Go to 35 
●​ Join business networking groups to find early 
opportunities. → Go to 36

sections.heading: 12. Borrowing from Friends and Family
sections.title: Borrowing from Friends and Family
sections.text:
You decide that banks and lenders aren’t the only option, you turn 
to friends and family for support. You craft a convincing pitch, 
explaining your business idea and how a little financial boost 
could help you succeed. Some are excited to help, while others 
raise skeptical eyebrows. After all, they’ve seen people chase big 
dreams before… and crash hard. 
Now comes the test. Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Your pitch is solid, and a few people believe in you 
enough to invest. You secure the funding and move 
forward. → Go to 37 
●​ 8-10 → You manage to convince someone, but the terms 
aren’t ideal, maybe they want a cut of your profits, or they 
expect repayment quickly. → Go to 38 
●​ 7 or below → No one is willing to take the risk on you. 
You’ll need to find another way to fund your business. → 
Go to 39

sections.heading: 13. Salvaging the Course Investment
sections.title: Salvaging the Course Investment
sections.text:
You take a deep breath and decide that even if the guru course 
wasn’t what you expected, there might still be some value hidden 
in there. You go through the lessons with a more critical eye, 
filtering out the fluff and focusing on actionable steps. 
You manage to pull some useful insights, such as niche 
selection strategies, sales psychology, or an idea for a digital 
product. However, the success of implementing these strategies 
depends on how well you adapt them to your business model. 
Now comes the test. Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You extract a genuinely useful strategy and use it 
to create a viable offer! → Go to 40 
●​ 8-10 → Some ideas work, but it’s a struggle. You gain 
small progress, but no major breakthrough. → Go to 41 
●​ 7 or below → Nothing useful. The course was a total 
waste, and you’re down $997. Time to pivot fast. → Go to 
42

sections.heading: 14. Cutting Your Losses and Pivoting
sections.title: Cutting Your Losses and Pivoting
sections.text:
You close your laptop, take a deep breath, and accept the hard 
truth, you got played. The guru’s course was nothing more than 
recycled fluff, and your $997 is gone. But rather than spiral into 
despair (or worse, buy another course from the same guy), you 
decide it’s time to pivot to a real business strategy. 
You need a new plan, and your mentor is here to help guide 
the way. 
If you chose The Bootstrapper 
"Forget the fancy courses. Real entrepreneurs build, test, and 
iterate. Let’s hustle and get some traction!" 
●​ Option 1: Start a service-based business immediately 
using skills you already have. No website, no overhead, 
just sell. → Go to 44 
●​ Option 2: Leverage free traffic by building an audience 
with content before launching an offer. → Go to 45 
If you chose The Hustler 
"Time to turn this setback into a win. You don’t need money, you 
need attention. Let’s go viral." 
●​ Option 1: Use organic marketing and viral content 
strategies to recover fast. → Go to 46 
●​ Option 2: Turn your failure into a story that builds 
authority, attracting an audience eager to learn from your 
mistake. → Go to 47 
If you chose The Deal Maker 
"Losing money is part of the game, but the best entrepreneurs 
know how to turn losses into leverage. Let’s negotiate." 
●​ Option 1: Form a strategic partnership with someone 
who has resources but needs your skills. → Go to 48 
●​ Option 2: Use industry connections to salvage 
something from the failed investment, maybe even 
negotiate a partial refund. → Go to 49 
No matter what, one thing is clear, you’re done chasing shortcuts. 
It’s time to build something real.

sections.heading: 15. Doubling Down on the Guru Path
sections.title: Doubling Down on the Guru Path
headingLines: 15. Doubling Down on the Guru Path
sections.text:
You hesitate. Maybe the first course wasn’t great, but what if you 
just didn’t implement it properly? The guru did say the real 
secrets were in his elite coaching program, and for only 
$4,997, you can get exclusive access to his inner circle. 
This is a massive investment, and part of you wonders if you’re 
about to be scammed again. But what if this really is the missing 
piece? What if the reason it didn’t work before was… you? 
The refund policy is suspiciously vague. There’s no turning back 
once you hit “buy.” 
 
Optional Gamble – The Guru’s “Elite Secrets” 
Before making your final decision, a thought creeps in. What if 
this is the golden ticket? 
You could go all in. Double down on the guru life. Risk it all for 
a massive shortcut to success. 
You can choose to take the High-Risk Guru Gamble. 
➡ Roll 2d6: 
●​ 12+ → Against all odds, it actually works! Turns out, 
there’s a kernel of truth in his teachings. You gain +2 
Tactics (TA) and $5,000 Capital. 
●​ 8-11 → Not life-changing, but not a total waste. You 
pick up a useful strategy (+1 Tactics TA) and make a 
valuable connection. 
●​ 7 or below → Total scam. You lose ALL Capital and 
must restart Act 1. 
 
If you took (or skipped) the gamble, it’s time to find out what 
happens with the course itself. 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → You scrape together something valuable from 
the course. Maybe it’s a hidden strategy buried in the 
fluff, or maybe just the realization that gurus don’t have 
all the answers, you do. Lose $4,997 but gain a critical 
business tactic. → Go to 50 
●​ 8-10 → The course is unimpressive, but at least you 
make a useful connection. Lose $4,997, but network 
with someone who could help later. → Go to 51 
●​ 7 or below → It’s all smoke and mirrors. The guru 
bounces with your money, leaving you with nothing but 
motivational fluff. Lose $4,997 and restart Act 1. → Go 
to 1 
The stakes have never been higher. Will you find a hidden 
gem inside the guru’s course… or lose everything?

sections.heading: 16. The Social Media Experiment
sections.title: The Social Media Experiment
sections.text:
You decide that the fastest way to get eyes on your business is 
through social media. You craft a few posts, share them across 
different platforms, and hit “Publish.” 
Now, you wait. Will people notice? Will anyone care? Or will your 
posts vanish into the void of zero likes and crickets? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Your content resonates! You get engagement, 
comments, and even a few potential customers reaching 
out. → Go to 55 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed results. Some likes, a few shares, but 
nothing groundbreaking. You gain small traction, but it’s 
slow. → Go to 56 
●​ 7 or below → Silence. Your posts barely get noticed, and 
your confidence takes a hit. Lose 1 point in Resilience. 
→ Go to 57 
Maybe this social media thing is harder than it looks. What’s 
your next move?

sections.heading: 17. Direct Outreach – Making the First Move
sections.title: Direct Outreach – Making the First Move
headingLines: 17. Direct Outreach – Making the First Move
sections.text:
You decide that waiting for customers to come to you isn’t a 
strategy, it’s a gamble. Instead, you take matters into your own 
hands and start reaching out to potential clients directly. 
Maybe you cold DM people on Instagram or LinkedIn, or 
maybe you email small business owners who might need your 
services. Either way, you brace yourself for responses, or lack 
thereof. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Success! A few people respond positively, and 
you land your first real business opportunity. → Go to 
58 
●​ 8-10 → Some interest, but no immediate sales. A few 
people respond, but most say "I’ll think about it." → Go to 
59 
●​ 7 or below → Rejection city. Most people ignore you, 
and the few who reply aren’t interested. → Go to 60 
Reaching out directly is tough, but it’s also one of the fastest 
ways to get momentum. The question is, how do you follow up 
from here?

sections.heading: 18. The Paid Ads Gamble
sections.title: The Paid Ads Gamble
sections.text:
You decide to skip the slow grind and get your business in front 
of potential customers fast by running paid ads. Facebook, 
Instagram, Google, you pick a platform, set a budget, and hit 
“Launch.” 
Now, you wait. Will your investment bring in sales, or will it vanish 
into the abyss of bad targeting and ignored ads? 
Roll 2d6 + Tech Savviness (TS): 
●​ 11+ → Jackpot! Your ads are well-targeted, and you start 
seeing leads and even a few sales. → Go to 61 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed results. You get some clicks but no real 
conversions yet. You learn a few things, but your budget 
is burning fast. → Go to 62 
●​ 7 or below → Disaster. You set the wrong budget, or 
your targeting is way off. You lose $500 in Capital. → Go 
to 63 
Paid ads can be a powerful tool, but they can also drain your 
budget fast if you don’t know what you’re doing. Do you double 
down, optimize, or pull back?

sections.heading:
19. Validating Your Offer – Talking to Real
Customers
sections.title: Validating Your Offer – Talking to Real Customers
headingLines: 19. Validating Your Offer – Talking to Real
sections.text:
You realize that before you invest any more time or money, you 
need real feedback. It’s time to talk to potential customers and 
validate whether your offer is actually something people want. 
You put together a quick survey, hop on calls, or engage in direct 
conversations with your target audience. What they say could 
change everything. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Strong validation! People love your idea, and 
some even pre-order. → Go to 64 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed feedback. Some people like it, but others 
raise concerns. → Go to 65 
●​ 7 or below → Bad news. People don’t seem interested at 
all. Your idea needs serious work. → Go to 66 
Validating your offer before launching could save you time and 
money, but it could also reveal hard truths about your idea.

sections.heading: 20. Crafting the Perfect Offer
sections.title: Crafting the Perfect Offer
sections.text:
Armed with research from real customers, you sit down to 
create an offer they can’t refuse. Pricing, bonuses, and how you 
position it all matter. 
But will your research-driven offer hit the mark, or fall flat? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Nailed it! Your offer aligns perfectly with customer 
needs, and people are eager to buy. → Go to 67 
●​ 8-10 → It’s solid but needs work. Some people show 
interest, but it’s not converting as fast as you hoped. → 
Go to 68 
●​ 7 or below → Something is off. Maybe it’s the price, the 
messaging, or just bad positioning. → Go to 69 
A well-crafted offer is the difference between a struggling 
startup and a business that thrives.

sections.heading:
21. The Fast-Track Approach – Skipping Research
and Selling Immediately
sections.title: The Fast-Track Approach – Skipping Research and Selling Immediately
sections.text:
Who needs research? Time is money, and while others waste 
hours on surveys, you take action. 
You craft an offer, set up a quick landing page, and start 
promoting immediately, no customer validation, no feedback 
loops, just pure execution. 
But will your bold move lead to instant success or a painful 
lesson? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 12+ (Critical Success!) → Instant breakthrough! Your 
gut instinct was 100% correct, and customers flock to 
buy. → Go to 266 
●​ 10-11 → Strong start. Your offer resonates, and you 
make a solid batch of early sales. → Go to 71 
●​ 7-9 → Uncertain outcome. You get some engagement 
but no real traction. People are interested, but not 
enough to buy. → Go to 72 
●​ 6 or below → Disaster. Your offer completely misses the 
mark, and you burn capital on ads, inventory, and 
branding with zero sales. → Go to 73 
Skipping research is a gamble, move fast, and you might strike 
gold… or go broke trying.

sections.heading: 22. The First Sale – A Game-Changing Moment
sections.title: The First Sale – A Game-Changing Moment
headingLines: 22. The First Sale – A Game-Changing Moment
sections.text:
After all the planning, stress, and second-guessing, you finally 
see it… a notification. 
You made your first sale. 
It’s a small amount, maybe just a single order, but it feels 
monumental, because it means your business is real. Someone 
out there, a stranger, believed in you enough to pay for what 
you created. 
 
Optional Gamble – The High-Stakes Reinvestment 
Before you celebrate too much, you get a crazy idea. 
What if you reinvest everything immediately, double down 
and turn this tiny win into something massive? 
You can choose to take the High-Risk Reinvestment Gamble. 
➡ Roll 2d6: 
●​ 12+ → Genius move! Your reinvestment pays off 
massively. Gain $7,500 Capital instead of $2,500. 
●​ 8-11 → Mixed results. You gain $1,500 instead of 
$2,500, not a disaster, but not ideal. 
●​ 7 or below → You went all in… and lost. The 
reinvestment backfires completely. Lose ALL Capital. 
Restart Act 1. 
 
Now whether you took the gamble or not you take a deep breath, 
savoring the moment. But now the real question is, what’s next? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Momentum builds! Word spreads, and more 
sales start rolling in. → Go to 74 
●​ 8-10 → Slow but steady. Your first sale doesn’t trigger 
an immediate rush, but it’s a start. → Go to 75 
●​ 7 or below → One-hit wonder? Your first sale is exciting 
but doesn’t lead to any more. You need to rethink your 
strategy. → Go to 76 
This first win is proof that your idea works, but now you have to 
turn one sale into many.

sections.heading:
23. Building on Early Success – Scaling or
Stumbling?
sections.title: Building on Early Success – Scaling or Stumbling?
headingLines: 23. Building on Early Success – Scaling or
sections.text:
With your first sale in the bag, you feel unstoppable. The 
question now is: how do you turn this into something bigger? 
You have a few options. You could double down on what 
worked, tweak your strategy to improve conversions, or even 
try something completely new. 
But scaling too fast or without a solid foundation could also 
backfire. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Breakthrough! You refine your approach, and 
sales double almost overnight. → Go to 77 
●​ 8-10 → Some progress, but not explosive growth. You 
make a few more sales, but scaling is harder than 
expected. → Go to 78 
●​ 7 or below → Overwhelmed! You scale too quickly or 
inefficiently, leading to missed orders, refunds, or ad 
overspending. → Go to 79 
Every business owner faces this moment, play it safe, or push 
forward aggressively.

sections.heading: 24. The Cold, Hard Silence – Facing the Crickets
sections.title: The Cold, Hard Silence – Facing the Crickets
headingLines: 24. The Cold, Hard Silence – Facing the Crickets
sections.text:
You refresh your inbox. Nothing. You check your website 
analytics. Still nothing. 
Your post? Ignored. Your ad? Burned through money without 
a single sale. 
You knew starting a business wouldn’t be easy, but you didn’t 
expect the universe to respond with… absolute silence. 
For a brief moment, you wonder if you should just quit and 
delete everything before anyone notices. But no, you’re better 
than that. Time to pivot. 
What’s your next move? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You adapt like a pro. You tweak your messaging, 
adjust your strategy, and find a much better angle. → Go 
to 83 
●​ 8-10 → You make a few small changes. Some things 
improve, but it’s still slow going. → Go to 84 
●​ 7 or below → Panic pivot. You throw everything at the 
wall, hoping something sticks… and end up wasting 
money. → Go to 85 
Entrepreneurship isn’t about never failing, it’s about failing fast 
and adjusting before you run out of cash.

sections.heading: 25. The Low-Risk Experiment – Testing the Waters
sections.title: The Low-Risk Experiment – Testing the Waters
headingLines: 25. The Low-Risk Experiment – Testing the Waters
sections.text:
After soaking up all that knowledge, you realize there’s only 
one way to know if you’re onto something, you have to test it. 
But instead of going all in, you decide to start small. Maybe it’s 
offering a beta version of your service, selling a limited quantity 
of a product, or launching a basic version of your idea before 
committing fully. 
Will this cautious approach pay off or just delay the inevitable? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Smart move! Your test run gets real interest, and 
people even start pre-ordering. → Go to 89 
●​ 8-10 → It’s a mixed bag. Some feedback is positive, 
some negative. You learn a lot but don’t make any real 
money yet. → Go to 90 
●​ 7 or below → False start. The small test fails to attract 
buyers, and you realize you need to rethink your idea. 
→ Go to 91 
Testing before fully committing is smart business, but only if you 
learn the right lessons.

sections.heading:
26. The Business Plan Debate – Overplanning or
Smart Strategy?
sections.title: The Business Plan Debate – Overplanning or Smart Strategy?
headingLines: 26. The Business Plan Debate – Overplanning or
sections.text:
You decide that before making any major moves, you need a 
rock-solid business plan. 
You map out everything, target audience, pricing strategy, growth 
projections, and even a marketing roadmap. You obsess over 
the details, making sure you’ve covered every possible angle 
before taking action. 
But here’s the thing… is this strategic preparation or just 
glorified procrastination? 
Roll 2d6 + Tech Savviness (TS): 
●​ 11+ → A masterpiece! Your business plan is airtight, and 
when you launch, everything runs smoothly. → Go to 92 
●​ 8-10 → Good… but slow. You’ve built a great plan, but in 
the time you took to perfect it, others have already 
started selling. → Go to 93 
●​ 7 or below → Analysis paralysis. You get stuck in 
planning mode, overthinking every decision. → Go to 94 
A plan helps guide success, but too much planning keeps you 
stuck on the sidelines.

sections.heading:
27. Seeking Your Mentor’s Help – The First Real
Test
sections.title: Seeking Your Mentor’s Help – The First Real Test
headingLines: 27. Seeking Your Mentor’s Help – The First Real
sections.text:
You decide that it’s time to stop struggling alone and actually 
put your mentor to use. After all, that’s what they’re here for, 
right? 
You reach out, explain your situation, and ask for their best 
advice on how to move forward. But will they steer you in the 
right direction, or will this just be another case of “Figure it out 
yourself”? 
If you chose The Bootstrapper: 
"Stop overthinking. Start doing. Right now." 
●​ Option 1: Launch a simple version of your offer 
immediately and refine it later. → Go to 98 
●​ Option 2: Hustle your way into a few quick sales 
through word-of-mouth marketing. → Go to 99 
If you chose The Hustler:

sections.heading:
28. The First Real Customers – Early Wins or More
Rejection?
sections.title: The First Real Customers – Early Wins or More Rejection?
headingLines: 28. The First Real Customers – Early Wins or More
sections.text:
You’ve put yourself out there, whether through social media, 
networking, cold outreach, or sheer persistence. Now, the 
moment of truth: Will anyone actually buy? 
Your heart races as you check your messages, emails, and 
notifications. Are you about to make real money, or are you 
just another hopeful entrepreneur shouting into the void? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Success! You land multiple customers who are 
excited about your offer. → Go to 104 
●​ 8-10 → Some interest, but no explosion of sales. A few 
customers buy, but it’s slower than expected. → Go to 
105 
●​ 7 or below → Total silence. No sales, no responses, just 
rejection. → Go to 106 
Early customers can make or break a business, but getting 
them is only the beginning.

sections.heading:
29. Stuck in Limbo – Not Quite a Success, Not
Quite a Failure
sections.title: Stuck in Limbo – Not Quite a Success, Not Quite a Failure
headingLines: 29. Stuck in Limbo – Not Quite a Success, Not
sections.text:
You’ve made some progress. A few people showed interest, 
maybe even a sale or two, but you’re not exactly raking in the 
cash. 
You’re officially in the awkward middle ground, too much 
traction to quit, but not enough to feel like you’ve really “made it.” 
So what now? Do you double down, tweak your approach, or 
rethink your whole strategy? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You refine your approach, and things start 
picking up. Maybe it’s adjusting pricing, improving 
messaging, or just sheer persistence, but whatever it is, 
it’s working. → Go to 110 
●​ 8-10 → Slight improvement, but still not a 
breakthrough. Some small wins keep you going, but 
you’re still searching for momentum. → Go to 111 
●​ 7 or below → You miscalculate and waste time on the 
wrong things. Instead of fixing the real issue, you 
overcomplicate everything. → Go to 112 
The hardest part of business isn’t starting, it’s figuring out what 
actually works and doing more of that.

sections.heading:
30. The Brutal Reality Check – Facing Rejection and
Moving Forward
sections.title: The Brutal Reality Check – Facing Rejection and Moving Forward
headingLines: 30. The Brutal Reality Check – Facing Rejection and
sections.text:
Silence. No sales. No interest. Nothing. 
Your offer is out there, and the market has spoken, and it has 
said “no thanks.” 
At this point, you could do what most people do: give up, blame 
the algorithm, and decide that entrepreneurship is a scam. 
Or, you can take the punch, get back up, and figure out what 
went wrong. 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → You analyze the failure, adjust your offer, and 
try again. This time, something clicks, and you start 
getting traction. → Go to 113 
●​ 8-10 → You tweak things and keep going, but the 
results are still slow. It’s not a total loss, but success still 
feels far away. → Go to 114 
●​ 7 or below → Frustration gets the best of you. You 
make desperate changes, waste money, and end up 
worse off than before. → Go to 115 
Every entrepreneur faces rejection. The ones who succeed? 
They’re the ones who keep going anyway.

sections.heading:
31. Smart Money – A Loan That Works in Your
Favor
sections.title: Smart Money – A Loan That Works in Your Favor
headingLines: 31. Smart Money – A Loan That Works in Your
sections.text:
You did it. You managed to secure funding on favorable terms, 
maybe it’s a small business loan, an investor who believes in 
you, or even a low-interest credit option. 
For once, things feel like they’re going your way. But now comes 
the real challenge, what do you do with the money? 
Gain $2000 Capital! 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Invest in marketing to get more eyes on your offer 
quickly. → Go to 116 
●​ Use the funds to improve your product/service before 
going all in. → Go to 117 
●​ Keep most of the loan as a financial cushion so you 
don’t run out of money too quickly.  → Go to 118 
A loan can be a blessing or a curse. Spend it wisely, and it fuels 
your success. Waste it? You’ll just be in debt with nothing to 
show for it.

sections.heading:
32. The Cost of Borrowing – Money with Strings
Attached
sections.title: The Cost of Borrowing – Money with Strings Attached
headingLines: 32. The Cost of Borrowing – Money with Strings
sections.text:
You got the money, but it wasn’t free. 
Maybe the interest rates are higher than expected, maybe your 
investor is breathing down your neck, or maybe the friend who 
lent you the cash keeps dropping hints about wanting their 
money back, soon. 
This funding comes with pressure, and now you need to start 
making money fast.​
​
Gain $1000 Capital but -1 to Tactics.  
What’s your next move? 
●​ Go aggressive, pump all the money into a big marketing 
push and hope for fast returns. → Go to 119 
●​ Play it safe, use the money in small, strategic ways to 
minimize risk. → Go to 120 
●​ Stall for time, delay repayment and hope you can earn 
enough before the pressure explodes → Go to 204 
 
Getting money is one thing, making sure it doesn’t bury you in 
stress is another.

sections.heading: 33. Rejected – No One Wants to Lend You Money
sections.title: Rejected – No One Wants to Lend You Money
headingLines: 33. Rejected – No One Wants to Lend You Money
sections.text:
You tried. You pitched your idea, filled out loan applications, 
maybe even begged a friend or two. 
And yet… nothing. 
Banks aren’t interested. Investors don’t see the potential. Your 
friends? They suddenly "don’t have the budget right now." 
Now you’re stuck with no extra funding and no choice but to 
figure out another way forward. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Bootstrap harder, cut every unnecessary cost and grind 
your way forward with what you have. → Go to 122 
●​ Look for a business partner who can bring in capital in 
exchange for equity. → Go to 123 
●​ Try crowdfunding, launch a campaign and see if 
strangers believe in your idea. → Go to 124 
No money? No problem. Plenty of businesses have started 
with nothing, if you’re willing to hustle.

sections.heading: 34. Finding Your Niche – Passion or Profits?
sections.title: Finding Your Niche – Passion or Profits?
headingLines: 34. Finding Your Niche – Passion or Profits?
sections.text:
After soaking up every free business lesson available, you realize 
something: you need a niche. 
Sure, you could just sell anything, but that’s how you end up 
being the person pushing “high-ticket drop-shipping” courses at 
family dinners. 
No, you need to pick something people actually want. 
So, do you follow your passion, chase the money, or try to 
blend both? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Perfect niche unlocked! You find an in-demand 
market that also excites you. → Go to 125 
●​ 8-10 → Decent choice, but not groundbreaking. You 
land on something viable, but it won’t make you rich 
overnight. → Go to 126 
●​ 7 or below → Total dud. You spend way too long 
researching and pick something no one actually wants. → 
Go to 127 
Choosing the right niche is like dating, pick the wrong one, and 
you’ll spend years wondering why you didn’t just go with your 
first instinct.

being the person pushing “high-ticket drop-shipping” courses at 
family dinners. 
No, you need to pick something people actually want. 
So, do you follow your passion, chase the money, or try to 
blend both? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Perfect niche unlocked! You find an in-demand 
market that also excites you. → Go to 125 
●​ 8-10 → Decent choice, but not groundbreaking. You 
land on something viable, but it won’t make you rich 
overnight. → Go to 126 
●​ 7 or below → Total dud. You spend way too long 
researching and pick something no one actually wants. → 
Go to 127 
Choosing the right niche is like dating, pick the wrong one, and 
you’ll spend years wondering why you didn’t just go with your 
first instinct.

MVP Approach
sections.title: Creating Your First Product or Service – The MVP Approach
headingLines: 35. Creating Your First Product or Service – The
sections.text:
After diving deep into free resources, you realize there’s only so 
much learning you can do before you actually build something. 
You don’t need a perfect product, you just need something good 
enough to sell. 
So, what will it be? A service you can offer? A digital product? 
Something physical? You whip out your notebook and start 
brainstorming. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You create a simple but powerful offer. It’s clear, 
valuable, and people love it. → Go to 134 
●​ 8-10 → It’s okay, but not amazing. You make something 
solid, but it still needs refining. → Go to 135 
●​ 7 or below → Overcomplicated mess. You get stuck in 
perfectionism hell, spending way too much time 
making it “just right.” → Go to 136 
A good business starts with a good offer, but too much 
overthinking can kill momentum.

sections.heading:
36. Networking for Opportunities – Connections or
Crickets?
sections.title: Networking for Opportunities – Connections or Crickets?
sections.text:
You realize that who you know can be just as important as 
what you know. So, instead of grinding away alone, you decide 
to put yourself out there and start building relationships. 
Maybe it’s joining an online community, attending networking 
events, or just sliding into LinkedIn DMs like a desperate 
intern. Either way, this is your shot to connect with the right 
people and open doors. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You make the right connections. Someone 
offers a partnership, a key referral, or even a first paying 
client. → Go to 137 
●​ 8-10 → You meet some interesting people, but no 
major breakthroughs. You build relationships, but 
nothing turns into immediate cash. → Go to 138 
●​ 7 or below → Networking nightmare. You either say 
something embarrassing, end up in a group full of 
time-wasters, or just get ignored completely. → Go to 
139 
Networking can open doors or waste time, depending on who 
you meet and how you use those connections.

sections.heading:
37. Friendly Investors – Family and Friends Come
Through
sections.title: Friendly Investors – Family and Friends Come Through
headingLines: 37. Friendly Investors – Family and Friends Come
sections.text:
You delivered a killer pitch, and a few people believe in your 
vision. Maybe it’s your uncle who always wanted to be an 
entrepreneur, your friend who made a bit of cash in crypto, or 
your parents who just don’t want to see you fail. 
Either way, you got the money. Now, you just have to use it 
wisely. 
Gain $2000 Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the funds for marketing to attract customers faster. 
→ Go to 140 
●​ Invest in improving your offer before trying to sell it. → 
Go to 141 
●​ Keep the cash as a safety net and focus on organic 
growth. → Go to 118 
A little extra capital can go a long way, if you don’t waste it.

sections.heading:
38. Strings Attached – The Cost of Borrowing from
People You Know
sections.title: Strings Attached – The Cost of Borrowing from People You Know
headingLines: 38. Strings Attached – The Cost of Borrowing from
sections.text:
You got the money, but it wasn’t free. 
Maybe they want a percentage of your profits, maybe they 
keep calling to check on their investment, or maybe they 
expect repayment way too soon. 
Suddenly, your business partner is also your mom, and that 
comes with some serious pressure. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Work twice as hard to pay them back quickly and get 
them off your back. → Go to 143 
●​ Try renegotiating the terms before things get awkward. 
→ Go to 144 
●​ Use the money as planned and hope they stay patient. 
→ Go to 145 
Borrowing from friends and family can be a shortcut to funding, 
or a shortcut to ruining relationships.

sections.heading:
39. No Luck – Your Friends and Family Just Aren’t
Buying It
sections.title: No Luck – Your Friends and Family Just Aren’t Buying It
headingLines: 39. No Luck – Your Friends and Family Just Aren’t
sections.text:
You pitched your heart out, but no one’s biting. 
Maybe they’re too skeptical, maybe they just don’t have the 
money, or maybe they just don’t believe you’re actually going 
to pull this off. 
Either way, you’re still broke, and now you need to figure out 
another way to fund your business. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Bootstrap even harder, cut every unnecessary cost and 
grind your way forward. → Go to 146 
●​ Seek out an investor or business partner who has 
money to contribute. → Go to 147 
●​ Try crowdfunding, see if strangers will back your idea. → 
Go to 124 
Rejection stings, but plenty of great businesses started with 
nothing. Time to get creative.

sections.heading: 40. Turning a Scam into a Strategy
sections.title: Turning a Scam into a Strategy
headingLines: 40. Turning a Scam into a Strategy
sections.text:
Surprisingly, not everything in the guru’s course was total 
garbage. Sure, most of it was motivational fluff, but you 
managed to dig out something useful, a niche selection trick, a 
better sales angle, or even just a solid marketing tactic. 
You take what works, ignore the nonsense, and apply it. And 
guess what? It actually pays off. 
Gain $2,000 in Capital. 
Now, what’s next? 
●​ Double down on this new strategy and refine it further. 
→ Go to 149 
●​ Start selling aggressively now that you’ve got a solid 
offer. → Go to 150 
●​ Test the waters carefully before going all in. → Go to 
151 
A bad investment doesn’t have to be a total loss, if you know 
how to pivot.

sections.heading: 41. A Struggle, But Not a Total Loss
sections.title: A Struggle, But Not a Total Loss
headingLines: 41. A Struggle, But Not a Total Loss
sections.text:
You sift through the guru’s nonsense and actually find a few 
decent insights, nothing groundbreaking, but enough to give 
you a starting point. 
You apply what you’ve learned, but it’s not an instant success. 
Some things work, others fall flat, and you feel like you’re 
stumbling through the dark. 
Still, progress is progress. 
Gain $500 in Capital. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Tweak your approach and try to improve your results. → 
Go to 152 
●​ Look for another strategy, this one isn’t quite clicking. → 
Go to 17 
●​ Take a break and regroup before pushing forward. → Go 
to 154 
Sometimes, the best business lessons come from figuring 
out what doesn’t work.

sections.heading: 42. A Total Waste – The Guru Got You Good
sections.title: A Total Waste – The Guru Got You Good
headingLines: 42. A Total Waste – The Guru Got You Good
sections.text:
You stare at your screen in disbelief. 
Every single module, every so-called "secret strategy," every 
"proven blueprint", all of it is useless. You might as well have 
paid $997 for a motivational speech from a guy standing next to a 
rented Lamborghini. 
And now, you're down almost a grand with nothing to show 
for it. 
This is the moment when most people quit. But you? You’re not 
most people. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Pivot fast, forget the course and find a real strategy. → 
Go to 155 
●​ Try and resell the course to someone else. → Go to 156 
●​ Go all in on free resources to make up for the loss. → 
Go to 157 
Sometimes, the best lesson in business is learning how to 
spot a scam.

sections.title: The Pivot – Moving on from a Bad Investment
headingLines: 43. The Pivot – Moving on from a Bad Investment
sections.text:
You shake off the frustration. Yeah, you lost money. Yeah, the 
guru scammed you. But wallowing in it won’t get you your 
money back. 
Instead, you take what little knowledge you did gain and pivot. 
Maybe you switch to a different niche, adjust your offer, or 
simply focus on a smarter strategy. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Brilliant move! Your pivot is exactly what was 
needed, and customers start responding. → Go to 158 
●​ 8-10 → It helps, but it’s not a game changer. You gain 
some traction but still struggle to scale. → Go to 159 
●​ 7 or below → Bad pivot. You change too much, confuse 
your audience, and lose valuable momentum. → Go to 
160 
A smart entrepreneur knows when to pivot, but a bad pivot can 
be just as dangerous as staying the course.

sections.heading:
44. The Service Hustle – Selling What You Already
Know
sections.title: The Service Hustle – Selling What You Already Know
headingLines: 44. The Service Hustle – Selling What You Already
sections.text:
No more fancy tactics, no more "secret formulas", it’s time to sell 
what you already know. 
You skip the fluff and start offering a service immediately. No 
website, no fancy branding, just straight hustle. 
Maybe you’re freelancing, consulting, coaching, or offering a 
done-for-you service. Whatever it is, the goal is simple: make 
money fast without overcomplicating it. 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Instant traction! You land multiple clients quickly, 
and cash starts flowing. → Go to 164 
●​ 8-10 → You get some clients, but it’s a grind. You’re 
making progress, but it’s not as easy as you thought. → 
Go to 165 
●​ 7 or below → Crickets. Nobody bites, and you realize 
selling a service isn’t as simple as it sounds. → Go to 
166 
Some people spend years trying to start a business. You? You 
just started. Now, can you make it work?

sections.heading: 45. The Long Game – Building an Audience First
sections.title: The Long Game – Building an Audience First
headingLines: 45. The Long Game – Building an Audience First
sections.text:
You decide to play it smart and strategic, instead of jumping 
straight into selling, you’ll build an audience first. 
No cold pitches. No awkward sales convos. Just valuable 
content that attracts the right people until they’re practically 
begging to buy from you. 
Maybe you start a YouTube channel, a blog, a podcast, or go 
all-in on social media. But will this slow-burn strategy pay off, 
or just burn you out? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You build momentum fast! People love your 
content, and you start growing a loyal audience. → Go to 
167 
●​ 8-10 → Some traction, but it’s slow. You’re getting 
engagement, but no real income yet. → Go to 168 
●​ 7 or below → Content flop. Either you picked the wrong 
platform, or your content just isn’t clicking. → Go to 169 
Building an audience takes time, but once you have it, selling 
becomes effortless. The question is, can you stick with it?

sections.heading: 46. Going Viral – Turning Attention Into Income
sections.title: Going Viral – Turning Attention Into Income
headingLines: 46. Going Viral – Turning Attention Into Income
sections.text:
Your mentor’s advice is clear: Forget playing it safe, it’s time to 
get LOUD. 
If you can get people talking, you can make sales. So, you go 
all in on organic marketing, viral content, and getting noticed 
fast. 
Maybe it’s a controversial take, a hilarious meme campaign, 
or a bold challenge that spreads like wildfire. Whatever it is, 
this is your make-or-break moment. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You explode overnight! Your content blows up, 
and sales follow. → Go to 170 
●​ 8-10 → Some buzz, but nothing crazy. You get 
engagement and some new followers, but sales are 
slow. → Go to 171 
●​ 7 or below → You misfire. Maybe it’s bad timing, the 
algorithm hates you, or people just don’t care. → Go to 
172 
Virality can change your business overnight, but betting on it 
can be risky. Will this be your breakout moment or just 
another internet flop?

sections.heading:
47. Turning Failure Into Authority – Make Your Loss
a Lesson
sections.title: Turning Failure Into Authority – Make Your Loss a Lesson
headingLines: 47. Turning Failure Into Authority – Make Your Loss
sections.text:
Your guru course disaster was embarrassing, but what if you 
turned it into an advantage? 
People love a comeback story, especially when it comes with 
valuable lessons. 
So, instead of hiding your mistake, you decide to lean into it. 
You create content about how you got scammed, what you 
learned, and how others can avoid the same mistake. 
Will your transparency win people over, or will they just see 
you as another failed entrepreneur? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → People love it. Your honesty builds trust, and 
suddenly, you’re the go-to person for business advice. 
→ Go to 173 
●​ 8-10 → Some engagement, but no major impact. A few 
people appreciate your honesty, but it’s not a game 
changer. → Go to 174 
●​ 7 or below → It backfires. Instead of building authority, 
you just look like another failed entrepreneur complaining 
online. → Go to 175 
Turning failure into credibility is an art, some people build 
empires on their losses, while others just end up as cautionary 
tales. Which one will you be?

sections.heading:
48. The Power of Partnerships – Leveraging
Someone Else’s Resources
sections.title: The Power of Partnerships – Leveraging Someone Else’s Resources
sections.text:
Your mentor reminds you: You don’t have to do this alone. 
Instead of struggling solo, you find someone with resources, 
connections, or capital, someone who needs your skills but 
doesn’t have the time or expertise to execute. 
A strategic partnership could shortcut your success, but will 
you find the right deal or just end up working for free? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You land a perfect partner. They bring funding, 
resources, or distribution, and suddenly, your 
business takes off. → Go to 176 
●​ 8-10 → You get a deal, but it’s not ideal. You gain some 
benefits, but your partner takes more control than you 
expected. → Go to 177 
●​ 7 or below → Bad partnership. You end up doing most 
of the work for little to no reward. → Go to 178 
The right partnership can fast-track your success. The wrong 
one? Just another bad business decision.

sections.heading:
49. Salvaging the Investment – Can You Get Your
Money Back?
sections.title: Salvaging the Investment – Can You Get Your Money Back?
headingLines: 49. Salvaging the Investment – Can You Get Your
sections.text:
Your mentor smirks. "A good entrepreneur never takes a loss 
without a fight." 
Instead of accepting defeat, you decide to try and get 
something back, maybe a partial refund, a credit for another 
course, or even just leverage the situation into an 
opportunity. 
Will you negotiate like a pro, or will the guru ghost you faster 
than an ex after a bad date? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Master negotiator! You convince the guru’s 
team to refund part of your investment or give you 
valuable access to another program. Gain $2,500 in 
Capital. → Go to 179 
●​ 8-10 → You get a little back. Maybe it’s a partial refund, 
access to some bonus material, or just enough to 
soften the loss. Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 180 
●​ 7 or below → No chance. They either ignore you, hit 
you with a no-refund policy, or gaslight you into 
thinking it’s your fault. Lose $500 in Capital (wasted 
time and energy). → Go to 181 
Sometimes, the art of business isn’t about making money, it’s 
about not losing it in the first place.

sections.heading: 50. Extracting a Sliver of Value – Was It Worth It?
sections.title: Extracting a Sliver of Value – Was It Worth It?
headingLines: 50. Extracting a Sliver of Value – Was It Worth It?
sections.text:
You’ve just dropped $4,997, and the moment you hit Confirm 
Payment, a wave of regret washes over you. 
You open the exclusive Inner Circle portal, bracing yourself. 
Module 1: Why the Poor Stay Poor (And Why It’s Their Fault!) 
(Yikes…)​
Module 2: How to Think Like a Billionaire (Even If You’re Flat 
Broke) (Okay, now I’m concerned…)​
Module 3: My 7-Step Wealth Manifestation Framework (That… 
literally means nothing.) 
You panic-scroll through the rest, searching for anything 
remotely useful, and then, buried in Module 14: Advanced 
Profit Tactics, you find it. 
A single nugget of actual wisdom. It’s not much, but it makes 
sense, a powerful sales technique, a pricing hack, or a 
negotiation strategy that could actually help. 
You grab a notepad and write it down. If you’re going to make 
back your money, this might be your only shot. 
Lose $4,997 in Capital. 
Gain +1 to Tactics (TA) – Your sales & negotiation skills just 
improved! 
Now what? 
●​ Use this newfound knowledge to refine your business 
and scale. → Go to 182 
●​ Try to recoup some of the money by implementing 
what you learned ASAP. → Go to 183 
●​ Admit you made a mistake and look for another way 
forward. → Go to 184 
You paid premium price for a single golden nugget, but 
sometimes, that’s all you need to turn things around. Will it be 
enough?

sections.heading:
51. A Costly Connection – Networking Your Way
Out of a Bad Decision
sections.title: A Costly Connection – Networking Your Way Out of a Bad Decision
headingLines: 51. A Costly Connection – Networking Your Way
sections.text:
The course itself? Garbage. Absolute hot, steaming garbage. 
You sit through hours of fluff, skimming useless modules with 
titles like "How to Align Your Energy With Success" and "The Law 
of Attraction is More Powerful Than Marketing." 
By Module 12, you’ve accepted you just burned $4,997… but 
then, something happens. 
Inside the Inner Circle community, you meet someone legit, a 
business owner who actually knows what they’re doing. 
Maybe it’s an experienced marketer, a high-level 
entrepreneur, or just someone with deep industry 
connections. They see potential in you, and suddenly, you’ve 
got a valuable new contact. 
Lose $4,997 in Capital. 
Gain +1 to Networking (NE) – You’ve leveled up your ability 
to connect with the right people. 
Now what? 
●​ Leverage this new connection to find new 
opportunities. → Go to 185 
●​ Ask your contact for help turning your business 
around. → Go to 186 
●​ Try to forget this entire financial disaster and move 
on. → Go to 187 
It wasn’t the wisest investment, but if you play it right, this one 
connection could open doors you never imagined.

sections.heading:
52. Upgrade & Relaunch – Second Shot at
Greatness
sections.title: Upgrade & Relaunch – Second Shot at Greatness
sections.text:
You dig into customer feedback like a startup founder reading 
Yelp reviews at midnight. Some of it stings ("the bonus was kinda 
meh"), but it’s honest, and that’s gold. 
You overhaul your offer: better onboarding, tighter bonuses, a 
clearer message, and a fresh sales page. You even fixed that 
typo that made it sound like you were offering “business coaching 
for dogs.” 
Now, it’s time to relaunch. Is this version 2.0 a hit, or just a 
polished version of something people still don’t want? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Nailed it! The upgrade hits perfectly. You get rave 
reviews, sales spike, and people are sharing it like it’s the 
next big thing.​
 Gain $3,000 in Capital. → Go to 243​
 
●​ 8–10 → Decent lift. The changes help, and people notice. 
More traction, more conversions, but not a full 
breakthrough.​
 Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 244​
 
●​ 7 or below → Polished but still not popping. The relaunch 
gets polite nods, but few buyers.​
 Lose $500 in Capital. → Go to 246

sections.heading: 53. Price Hike – Will They Pay More?
sections.title: Price Hike – Will They Pay More?
headingLines: 53. Price Hike – Will They Pay More?
sections.text:
You’ve proven your value. The testimonials are rolling in, the 
delivery is solid, and let’s be honest, you’re undercharging. 
So you do what every smart entrepreneur eventually must: raise 
your prices. 
You adjust the numbers, update your sales page, and take a 
deep breath. Will your audience see the added value, or will they 
vanish like your confidence after hitting “Publish”? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Success! Customers see the value and pay 
without hesitation. You make more money while working 
less.​
 Gain $3,000 in Capital. → Go to 243​
 
●​ 8–10 → Some pushback, but enough people buy at the 
new price to make it worth it.​
 Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 244​
 
●​ 7 or below → Nope. Crickets. Your audience ghosts you 
like it’s a bad Tinder date.​
 Lose $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 246​

sections.heading:
54. Evergreen Machine – Selling While You Sleep
(Sort Of)
sections.title: Evergreen Machine – Selling While You Sleep (Sort Of)
headingLines: 54. Evergreen Machine – Selling While You Sleep
sections.text:
You’ve delivered your offer, the feedback’s solid, and now you're 
ready to enter the promised land of passive income. 
You package up everything: the content, onboarding, bonuses, 
even that bonus video where your dog barked halfway through 
(you left it in for “authenticity”). 
You set up an evergreen funnel: ads, email automations, 
retargeting. It's not 100% passive, let's be real, but it runs while 
you sleep, and sales trickle in on autopilot. 
Gain $2,500 in Capital. 
What’s your next strategic move? 
●​ Scale the funnel by reinvesting ad profits and optimizing 
conversion rates. → Go to 205​
 
●​ Create a second offer to increase average order value 
and lifetime customer revenue. → Go to 70​
 
●​ Focus on nurturing your audience with content to build 
long-term brand loyalty. → Go to 196​

sections.heading:
55. Social Media Success – The Algorithm Smiles
Upon You
sections.title: Social Media Success – The Algorithm Smiles Upon You
headingLines: 55. Social Media Success – The Algorithm Smiles
sections.text:
For once, the social media gods have blessed your content. 
Your post takes off, likes, shares, comments. Maybe it’s a viral 
tweet, a high-value LinkedIn post, or a TikTok that gets 
stitched by someone famous. Whatever it is, people are 
engaging. 
Even better? A few potential customers slide into your DMs. 
It’s not quite a flood of sales, but it’s the kind of momentum 
that can snowball. 
Gain +1 to Networking (NE) – More people now recognize 
you as someone worth paying attention to. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Capitalize on the traction by launching an offer right 
now. → Go to 188 
●​ Double down on content to keep growing your audience 
before selling. → Go to 189 
●​ Reach out to your new followers and start building 
relationships. → Go to 190 
You’ve cracked the first level of social media success. The 
real challenge? Keeping the momentum going.

headingLines: 56. The “Meh” Response – Some Traction, But No
sections.text:
You hit publish. You wait. 
A few hours later, you check back… and there’s activity! A 
handful of likes, a couple of shares, and maybe even a 
comment from your mom saying how proud she is. 
It’s not a viral sensation, but hey, at least it’s not total crickets. 
Some people engage, a few DM you with questions, but there’s 
no massive rush of customers. 
This is what real marketing looks like, slow, steady, and built 
over time. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Analyze the results and tweak your approach for better 
engagement. → Go to 191 
●​ Stick with it and keep posting consistently. → Go to 192 
●​ Pivot to a different marketing strategy, maybe social 
media isn’t your strength. → Go to 193 
Social media isn’t a magic bullet. But if you play it right, it 
could become your most powerful asset.

sections.heading: 57. The Void – Social Media Ghost Town
sections.title: The Void – Social Media Ghost Town
headingLines: 57. The Void – Social Media Ghost Town
sections.text:
You hit publish. You wait. 
A few hours later, you check back… and nothing. 
Not a like. Not a comment. Not even a bot offering you “5,000 
real followers” for $19.99. 
You refresh the page, just in case. Still nothing. 
Your confidence takes a hit. Maybe you didn’t phrase it right? 
Maybe the algorithm hates you? Or maybe, just maybe… this 
social media thing is a little harder than those marketing 
gurus made it sound. 
Lose 1 point in Resilience (RE) – Failure stings, but will you 
push through? 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Study what’s working for others and reverse-engineer 
their success. → Go to 195 
●​ Say "screw it" and pivot to a different marketing 
strategy. → Go to 18 
●​ Boost the post with paid ads to force some 
engagement → Go to 207 
Social media might be free, but success here definitely comes 
at a cost, mostly, your sanity.

sections.heading:
58. The Follow-Up Game – Turning Interest into
Sales
sections.title: The Follow-Up Game – Turning Interest into Sales
headingLines: 58. The Follow-Up Game – Turning Interest into
sections.text:
Some people actually responded to your messages, which is a 
win in itself. 
The bad news? Most of them said “I’ll think about it” (aka, 
business limbo). 
Now, it’s time to follow up like a pro. But how? Do you go for 
the hard sell, build a relationship, or pivot to a different 
approach? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → You follow up masterfully. A few prospects 
convert into paying customers. → Go to 200 
●​ 8-10 → Some progress, but no major breakthroughs. 
A few leads stay interested, but no immediate sales. → 
Go to 201 
●​ 7 or below → You overdo it. Either you followed up too 
aggressively or just caught them at the wrong time. → 
Go to 18 
Sales is a long game, some people buy immediately, some take 
months, and some just ghost you forever. The trick is knowing 
when to push and when to move on.

sections.heading:
59. The Cold Outreach Struggle – Nobody’s
Buying… Yet
sections.title: The Cold Outreach Struggle – Nobody’s Buying… Yet
sections.text:
You’ve sent messages. Lots of them. 
Some people actually responded, but it’s mostly lukewarm 
interest at best. 
The dreaded “I’ll think about it” floods your inbox. Others just 
hit you with the classic thumbs-up emoji, which might as well be 
a digital shrug. 
You’re getting some traction, but no immediate wins. The real 
question is: what’s your next move? 
Gain $500 in Capital. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Keep following up, most sales happen after the second 
or third touch. → Go to 202 
●​ Tweak your messaging and try again with a refined 
approach. → Go to 203 
●​ Decide this isn’t working and pivot to another 
strategy. → Go to 18 
Sales is a numbers game, but at what point do you stop 
chasing leads and start looking elsewhere?

sections.heading:
60. Rejection City – The Harsh Reality of Cold
Outreach
sections.title: Rejection City – The Harsh Reality of Cold Outreach
headingLines: 60. Rejection City – The Harsh Reality of Cold
sections.text:
Well… that was brutal. 
Most of your messages were ignored. The few responses you 
got? Hard nos, vague excuses, or people asking if you take 
exposure as payment. 
One person even replied with "lol, no." (Ouch.). 
You stare at your inbox, questioning every life decision that led 
you here. 
Lose 1 point in Resilience (RE) – This one stings. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Decide this method isn’t working and try a different 
strategy. → Go to 18 
●​ Double down, refine your pitch and send twice as 
many messages → Go to 209 
●​ Step back and regroup before trying again → Go to 
214 
Rejection is part of the game, but can you bounce back, or 
will you let this kill your momentum?

61. Paid Ads Win – The Money Machine Starts
Turning
sections.title: Paid Ads Win – The Money Machine Starts Turning
headingLines: 61. Paid Ads Win – The Money Machine Starts
sections.text:
For once, the algorithm gods smile upon you. 
Your ad is well-targeted, the messaging clicks, and the leads 
start rolling in. Even better? You actually get a few sales. 
The rush of seeing money come in while you sleep makes you 
seriously consider quitting everything and going full digital 
nomad. 
Gain $2,000 in Capital. 
Now what? 
●​ Scale up your ad spend to bring in even more sales. → 
Go to 205 
●​ Optimize your ads first before spending more money. → 
Go to 206 
●​ Hand everything over to an agency and hope they scale 
it for you → Go to 222 
Paid ads can scale fast, but one wrong move and you’re 
burning money instead of making it. How aggressive do you 
want to go?

sections.heading: 62. The Learning Curve – Ads Are Tricky
sections.title: The Learning Curve – Ads Are Tricky
headingLines: 62. The Learning Curve – Ads Are Tricky
sections.text:
Well… it’s not a total disaster, but it’s not a home run either. 
Your ads are getting clicks, but no real conversions yet. Maybe 
your targeting is slightly off, maybe your landing page isn’t 
convincing enough, or maybe people just aren’t ready to buy. 
Either way, your budget is burning fast. 
You’ve learned a few things, but now you need to decide what 
to do next. 
No Capital gain or loss, yet. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Tweak your targeting and ad copy to improve 
performance. → Go to 208 
●​ Cut your losses and switch to a different marketing 
method. → Go to 17 
●​ Invest in a course or mentor to help you figure ads 
out faster → Go to 223 
Paid ads can be a goldmine, or a money pit. Right now, you’re 
standing right on the edge.

sections.heading:
63. The Ad Budget Disaster – Money Down the
Drain
sections.title: The Ad Budget Disaster – Money Down the Drain
headingLines: 63. The Ad Budget Disaster – Money Down the
sections.text:
Oh no. 
The moment you check your ad performance dashboard, your 
stomach drops. 
Your clicks? Almost nonexistent.​
 Your engagement? Minimal.​
 Your conversions? What conversions? 
It turns out running paid ads isn’t just about throwing money 
at the internet and hoping for the best. Your targeting was off, 
your ad copy didn’t land, or maybe you accidentally set the 
budget way too high, and Facebook happily took every cent. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Abandon paid ads and try a different marketing 
approach. → Go to 17 
●​ Try to salvage the campaign by quickly fixing your 
targeting → Go to 238 
●​ Pause the campaign and study the data before trying 
again → Go to 239 
Paid ads can scale a business fast, but they can also wipe out 
your budget before you even get started.

sections.heading:
64. Strong Validation – Customers Want What
You’re Selling!
sections.title: Strong Validation – Customers Want What You’re Selling!
sections.text:
You pitch your idea, expecting some polite nods and vague 
enthusiasm… but instead, people actually love it. 
Even better? A few of them pull out their wallets on the spot. 
Whether it’s pre-orders, deposits, or early sign-ups, you’ve got 
your first paying customers. It’s not just a business idea 
anymore, it’s real. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the money to start fulfilling orders and refining 
your product/service. → Go to 210 
●​ Invest in marketing to get even more customers. → 
Go to 211 
●​ Celebrate early success by pulling money out for 
yourself → Go to 249 
You just proved that your idea has demand. Now, can you 
deliver on it?

sections.heading: 65. Mixed Feedback – Some Love It, Some Don’t
sections.title: Mixed Feedback – Some Love It, Some Don’t
headingLines: 65. Mixed Feedback – Some Love It, Some Don’t
sections.text:
Well, that was... eye-opening. 
Some people loved your idea, they saw the value, they got 
excited, and they might even buy eventually. 
But others? Brutally honest. 
●​ “I don’t think I’d pay for this.” 
●​ “I’ve seen something similar, but cheaper.” 
●​ “Cool idea, but I wouldn’t use it.” 
Ouch. Not exactly the validation you were hoping for. 
The good news? You got useful insights. The bad news? No 
immediate sales. 
No Capital gain or loss, just valuable feedback. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Tweak your offer based on what you learned and test 
again. → Go to 212 
●​ Ignore the feedback and push forward anyway. → Go 
to 213 
●​ Run a low-cost test campaign to see how the market 
really reacts. → Go to 255 
Sometimes, the difference between success and failure is 
listening to the right feedback. Do you adapt or stay the 
course?

headingLines: 66. Hard Truths – Your Offer Needs Work
sections.text:
Well, that didn’t go as planned. 
You pitched your idea with hope in your heart, but the 
responses? Brutal.

●​ "I wouldn’t pay for that." 
●​ "Wait, this is a business idea? I thought you were joking." 
Ouch. 
Your gut sinks as you realize your brilliant offer might not be as 
brilliant as you thought. Time to go back to the drawing 
board. 
Lose $500 in Capital (wasted on market research, testing, 
and existential crises). 
What’s your next move? 
●​ You decide you need to learn more before moving 
forward. → Go to 8 
●​ Scrap the idea entirely and brainstorm something new 
from scratch. → Go to 262 
●​ Tweak your positioning instead of the product → Go 
to 263 
Some entrepreneurs push through with bad ideas. The smart 
ones? They learn, adapt, and make something people 
actually want. Which one are you?

sections.heading: 68. A Solid Start – But It’s Not a Sellout Hit
sections.title: A Solid Start – But It’s Not a Sellout Hit
headingLines: 68. A Solid Start – But It’s Not a Sellout Hit
sections.text:
Your offer is good, but not great. 
Some people love it and buy right away. Others? Hesitant. 
Maybe the price feels a little too high, or maybe they just need 
more convincing.​
​
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 9+ = Your side hustle gains traction → continue as 
written.​
 
●​ 8 or less = The idea flops → go to 95.​
 
You’re making some sales, but it’s not converting as fast as 
you hoped. 
No Capital gain or loss, just a lesson in refining your pitch. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Adjust the offer based on feedback to improve 
conversions. → Go to 217 
●​ Push forward without tweaking anything, maybe more 
marketing will fix it. → Go to 218 
A good offer can make money, but a great offer prints money. 
Are you willing to tweak it until it’s perfect?

headingLines: 69. The Offer Flop – Something’s Not Clicking
sections.text:
You had high hopes, but something’s… off. 
Maybe the price is too high. Maybe the messaging isn’t 
resonating. Maybe people just don’t see the value. 
You watch as your carefully crafted offer sits there, collecting 
more dust than dollars. 
It’s time to make some changes, fast. 
Lose $500 in Capital (testing new strategies, tweaking 
pricing, and attempting fixes). 
What’s your next move? 
●​ You decide to go back and validate your offer again 
with real customers. → Go to 19 
A weak offer won’t sell, no matter how good your marketing is. 
The question is, can you turn this around before you run out 
of cash?

sections.heading: 70. The Second Offer – More Value, More Revenue?
sections.title: The Second Offer – More Value, More Revenue?
headingLines: 70. The Second Offer – More Value, More Revenue?
sections.text:
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 7+ = You identify a promising audience → continue 
reading below.​
 
●​ 6 or less = You completely misread the market → go to 
96 
Your evergreen funnel is humming along, but you know what 
smart entrepreneurs do next? Sell more stuff to the people who 
already bought. 
You brainstorm an upsell, a companion product, or maybe even a 
“pro” version of your original offer. It’s fast, it’s lean, and it fits 
perfectly into your current funnel. 
You plug it in and wait for the results. Will your second offer boost 
your revenue, or confuse your audience and clutter your flow? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → It’s a hit! Your second offer increases customer 
value, boosts profit, and makes your funnel a 
money-printing machine.​
 Gain $3,000 in Capital. → Go to 240​
 
●​ 8–10 → Solid add-on. Some customers bite, others don’t, 
but it brings in extra revenue without breaking your funnel.​
 Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 241​
 
●​ 7 or below → Backfire. The second offer confuses buyers 
or distracts from the main one.​
 Lose $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 242​

Go to 219 
●​ Pause and refine the backend before ramping up 
sales. → Go to 220

Go to 267

keep up the momentum?

sections.heading: 72. Lukewarm Response – Interest, But No Sales
sections.title: Lukewarm Response – Interest, But No Sales
headingLines: 72. Lukewarm Response – Interest, But No Sales
sections.text:
You moved fast, got your offer out there, and… people noticed! 
But here’s the problem, they’re not buying. 
You’re getting clicks, shares, and comments, but nobody is 
actually pulling out their wallet. Maybe the price is off? Maybe 
they need more trust? Or maybe… you just skipped too many 
steps. 
No Capital gain or loss, just confusion and frustration. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Tweak your offer and messaging to push people over 
the edge. → Go to 221 
●​ Decide this approach isn’t working and go back to 
validate your offer properly. → Go to 19 
●​ Run a flash discount or bonus to tip the fence-sitters 
into buying. → Go to 268 
Taking fast action can work wonders, but only if people 
actually buy. Can you salvage this before it flops?

headingLines: 73. The Fast-Track Disaster – Burning Money for
sections.text:
Oh no. 
You skipped research, trusted your gut, and went all in. 
And it completely flopped. 
No sales. No engagement. Just a painful realization that you

sections.heading: 75. Slow But Steady – A Small Step Forward
sections.title: Slow But Steady – A Small Step Forward
headingLines: 75. Slow But Steady – A Small Step Forward
sections.text:
You stare at your screen, waiting for the rush of new sales to 
come flooding in. 
And… nothing. 
Your first sale was a great start, but it didn’t trigger an 
avalanche. No viral word-of-mouth. No sudden surge in demand. 
Just one lonely order sitting in your dashboard. 
Still, it’s proof that people will pay for what you’re offering. 
Now, you just have to figure out how to get more of them. 
Gain $500 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Double down on marketing to bring in more 
customers. → Go to 221 
●​ Reach out to your first customer and get their 
feedback. → Go to 225 
One sale isn’t a business, but it’s a start. The question is, where 
do you go from here?

sections.heading: 76. The One-Hit Wonder – No Repeat Sales
sections.title: The One-Hit Wonder – No Repeat Sales
headingLines: 76. The One-Hit Wonder – No Repeat Sales
sections.text:
You did it. You made a sale. 
And then… silence. 
No second order. No referrals. No sudden flood of interest. Just 
one lonely purchase sitting in your account like a participation 
trophy. 
Something isn’t clicking. Either people aren’t coming back, or 
they weren’t excited enough to tell others. 
On the bright side, you technically made money. A whopping 
$27. That’s enough for… half a tank of gas? A cheap dinner? 
A single overpriced latte at an airport? 
Gain $27 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Analyze what went wrong and tweak your offer or 
sales process. → Go to 226 
●​ Try a different marketing approach to bring in more 
buyers. → Go to 17 
●​ Double down on “hype” and try to push the same 
offer harder. → Go to 269 
Making a one-off sale is nice, but if you don’t figure out how to 
get repeatable success, you’re in trouble.

sections.heading: 77. Breakthrough! Sales Are Taking Off
sections.title: Breakthrough! Sales Are Taking Off
sections.text:
You tweak your offer, optimize your process, and suddenly, 
boom! 
Sales double overnight. Maybe it’s word-of-mouth, maybe your 
messaging finally clicked, or maybe the universe just decided to 
cut you a break. Either way, you’re watching orders roll in faster 
than you ever expected. 
Your inbox is full of payment notifications, your phone won’t 
stop buzzing, and for a moment, you think: Is this what being a 
millionaire feels like? 
Gain $3,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Ride the wave and invest even more into growth. → 
Go to 227 
●​ Pause and make sure your business can handle the 
demand before scaling further. → Go to 228 
●​ Take the win as validation and launch a brand-new 
offer immediately. → Go to 274 
Scaling is exciting, but dangerous. Do you go all in, or do you 
play it smart?

sections.heading: 78. Slow and Steady – Progress, But No Fireworks
sections.title: Slow and Steady – Progress, But No Fireworks
headingLines: 78. Slow and Steady – Progress, But No Fireworks
sections.text:
Well… it’s not exactly overnight success, but hey, progress is 
progress. 
You’re making consistent sales, and things are moving in the 
right direction. But it’s clear that scaling isn’t as simple as 
flipping a switch. 
Some days feel like big wins, others feel like you’re dragging 
your business uphill while it kicks and screams. 
Still, you’re growing, and that’s what matters. 
Gain $500 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Double down and push for aggressive scaling. → Go 
to 227 
●​ Step back and refine your processes before going 
bigger. → Go to 228 
●​ Try experimenting with a brand-new traffic channel. → 
Go to 275 
Success isn’t always flashy, but slow growth beats no 
growth, as long as you don’t get stuck in place.

sections.heading: 79. Scaling Too Fast – The Growing Pains Hit Hard
sections.title: Scaling Too Fast – The Growing Pains Hit Hard
headingLines: 79. Scaling Too Fast – The Growing Pains Hit Hard
sections.text:
You charged ahead, ready to scale like a boss. More ads. More 
customers. More everything. 
And then… it all goes sideways. 
●​ Your supplier is delayed. 
●​ Your customer support is overwhelmed. 
●​ Someone requested a refund. (Rude.) 
●​ You accidentally spent WAY too much on ads. 
Turns out, scaling isn’t just about selling more, it’s about 
keeping up with the growth. Right now? You’re barely holding it 
together. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
Clearly, something isn’t working. Instead of throwing more 
money at the problem, you take a deep breath and decide it’s 
time to go back to basics before this whole thing collapses. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Go back and focus on direct outreach to stabilize your 
revenue stream. → Go to 17 
●​ Revisit your offer and make sure it’s actually ready to 
scale. → Go to 19 
●​ Patch the leaks on the fly and try to keep scaling 
anyway. → Go to 276 
Sometimes, the best way forward is a step back. Will you 
refine your sales process or fix your offer before trying 
again?

sections.title: The Viral Surge – When the Internet Loves You
headingLines: 80. The Viral Surge – When the Internet Loves You
sections.text:
Your post takes off like wildfire. Shares, comments, and DMs 
flood in, and suddenly, you’re the center of attention. 
People love what you’re saying, and best of all? They’re 
buying. This could be the breakthrough moment you’ve been 
waiting for. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Ride the momentum and turn this into a proper 
launch. → Go to 228 
●​ Double down on engagement and interact with 
everyone who commented. → Go to 229 
●​ Try to force the virality into paid ads and hope 
lightning strikes twice. → Go to 277

your life. 
At least you’ve proven people care, you just need to figure out 
how to turn this engagement into real sales. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Follow up with commenters and turn them into leads. 
→ Go to 17 
●​ Rework your offer to better fit what people responded 
to. → Go to 19 
●​ Take the small buzz as proof you’re ready to scale 
with ads. → Go to 278
