sections.title: The Backlash – When the Internet Turns On You
headingLines: 82. The Backlash – When the Internet Turns On You
sections.text:
Well… that didn’t go as planned. 
Your post backfires spectacularly. Instead of attracting 
customers, you’ve attracted… trolls. Lots of trolls. 
You try to do damage control, but the comments section is a 
dumpster fire. Worse, your ad spend got wasted on people who 
just want to argue with you. 
What’s your best option now? Pivot 
●​ Salvage what’s left and tweak your messaging to try 
again. → Go to 19 
●​ Cut your losses and pivot to another marketing 
strategy. → Go to 17 
●​ Fight back against the trolls and double down to 
“prove them wrong.” → Go to 279

 Your ads? Finally converting.​

sections.title: Small Wins, But No Breakthroughs
sections.text:
You make a few adjustments, tweaking your messaging, testing a 
new audience, maybe even trying a different marketing angle.

the flood of customers you were hoping for. 
Your business is still alive, but it feels like you’re pushing a 
boulder uphill in slow motion. 
No Capital gain or loss, just a lesson in patience. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ You realize the key to getting more traction is refining 
your offer and making it irresistible. → Go to 19 
●​ You decide to focus on direct outreach to get in front 
of the right people faster. → Go to 17 
Some businesses take off like rockets. Others require a bit 
more grinding. Which path will you take?

sections.heading:
85. The Panic Pivot – Throwing Money at the
Problem
sections.title: The Panic Pivot – Throwing Money at the Problem
headingLines: 85. The Panic Pivot – Throwing Money at the
sections.text:
The silence was too much to handle. 
So, in a moment of pure desperation, you tried everything. 
●​ You ran a last-minute ad campaign (with zero strategy). 
●​ You offered a discount so big it practically screamed 
"I’m desperate!" 
●​ You rewrote your sales page five times in one night, 
convinced that a single word was the problem. 
And now? You’re down $1,000 in Capital… and not much better 
off than before. 
Panic-pivoting rarely works, but at least now you know what not 
to do. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Take a step back, validate your offer properly, and 
make sure it actually resonates. → Go to 19 
●​ Realize you need to focus on sales, not random 
tactics, and go back to direct outreach. → Go to 17 
Sometimes, the best way to move forward is to stop throwing 
spaghetti at the wall. What’s your next move?

sections.heading: 86. The Smooth Climb – Scaling Without the Stress
sections.title: The Smooth Climb – Scaling Without the Stress
headingLines: 86. The Smooth Climb – Scaling Without the Stress
sections.text:
Your decision to slow down and stabilize? Total win. 
Customers are happy. Deliveries are seamless. Your inbox isn’t 
on fire. You're making money and sleeping at night, an 
entrepreneurial miracle. 
Even better? Word-of-mouth starts picking up. People are tagging 
you, recommending you, and coming back for more. You’ve gone 
from “scrappy startup energy” to “quietly confident operator.” 
Now it’s time to decide how to scale this machine. 
Gain $3,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the momentum to confidently launch a paid ad 
campaign. → Go to 205​
 
●​ Create a backend offer or upsell to increase customer 
value. → Go to 54​
 
●​ Focus on building content and community to grow 
organically. → Go to 196

sections.heading: 87. Steady Progress – Slow, But in Control
sections.title: Steady Progress – Slow, But in Control
headingLines: 87. Steady Progress – Slow, But in Control
sections.text:
Things are running… fine. 
Not fireworks. Not crickets. Just slow, steady progress. You’ve 
fixed a few backend issues, improved your processes, and while 
you’re not going viral, you’re not stressed either. 
You’ve bought yourself breathing room, but you know this pace 
won’t take you to $10K anytime soon. 
Time to make a decision: Do you stay on this careful path, or is it 
time to be a little bolder? 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Take a bold risk and launch a new, higher-ticket offer. → 
Go to 245​
 
●​ Stick to what’s working and gradually grow your customer 
base. → Go to 168​
 
●​ Focus on long-term customer retention and referrals. → 
Go to 224

sections.heading: 88. Stuck in Setup Mode – Losing Speed
sections.title: Stuck in Setup Mode – Losing Speed
headingLines: 88. Stuck in Setup Mode – Losing Speed
sections.text:
You’ve spent so much time fixing systems, polishing automations, 
and perfecting onboarding that you forgot one important thing… 
to sell. 
The momentum you had? Gone. Website traffic is flat, your inbox 
is silent, and your ad account hasn’t seen activity in days. On the 
bright side, your backend is immaculate. 
Now you’re at a crossroads. You can keep building in silence, or 
snap yourself out of it and start making moves again. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Take a bold step and relaunch with a big offer to regain 
momentum. → Go to 245​
 
●​ Reconnect with past leads and customers to re-ignite 
interest. → Go to 59​
 
●​ Start fresh with a brand-new audience or offer. → Go to 
226​

sections.heading: 89. The Test Run Pays Off – Early Wins
sections.title: The Test Run Pays Off – Early Wins
headingLines: 89. The Test Run Pays Off – Early Wins
sections.text:
Your low-risk experiment turns out to be a brilliant move. 
People love what you’re offering, and some are even 
pre-ordering before the full launch. It’s proof that your idea has 
legs, and better yet, you just made money before going all in. 
It’s a huge confidence boost, and for the first time, you’re 
starting to see this business could actually work. 
Gain $2,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the momentum to go all-in on scaling up. → Go to 
227 
●​ Pause and refine your product or service before 
committing fully. → Go to 228 
A little smart testing goes a long way. But do you strike while 
the iron’s hot or play it smart and refine first?

sections.heading: 90. Mixed Results – Some Wins, Some Doubts
sections.title: Mixed Results – Some Wins, Some Doubts
headingLines: 90. Mixed Results – Some Wins, Some Doubts
sections.text:
Your test run didn’t flop… but it didn’t exactly take off either. 
Some people liked what you offered, others had concerns, and 
a few just ignored it altogether. You’re getting useful feedback, 
but no real money yet. 
It’s a reminder that business isn’t just about launching, it’s 
about adjusting. 
No Capital gain or loss, just valuable lessons. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the feedback to refine your offer and make it 
irresistible. → Go to 19 
●​ Go back to direct outreach to find customers who 
actually want what you’re offering. → Go to 17 
You’ve got something with potential, but potential doesn’t pay 
the bills. Do you tweak the offer or find the right audience?

sections.heading: 91. False Start – The Test Flops
sections.title: False Start – The Test Flops
sections.text:
Well… that didn’t go as planned. 
Your test run was supposed to give you a taste of success 
before fully committing. Instead, it gave you a harsh reality 
check. 
●​ Barely any interest. 
●​ No sales. 
●​ A lot of people just… didn’t care. 
You didn’t lose everything, but you’re now $1,000 lighter and 
questioning everything. Was this the wrong idea? Or just the 
wrong approach? 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Go back and refine your offer before trying again. → 
Go to 19 
●​ Realize you need to focus on sales, not just ideas, 
and start doing direct outreach. → Go to 17 
Setbacks aren’t the end, but they’re expensive if you don’t learn 
from them. What’s your next move?

sections.heading: 92. The Master Plan Pays Off – Smooth Execution
sections.title: The Master Plan Pays Off – Smooth Execution
headingLines: 92. The Master Plan Pays Off – Smooth Execution
sections.text:
Your business plan is a work of art. 
Everything is mapped out perfectly, from your target audience 
to your growth strategy. When you finally launch, it’s like 
clockwork. No scrambling, no last-minute chaos, just a 
well-executed strategy that actually works. 
Sales start rolling in immediately. It’s almost like… planning 
actually works? Who knew? 
Gain $2,500 in Capital. 
And because you were so prepared, your mentor actually 
gives you a bonus perk: 
🔹 If you chose The Bootstrapper: You planned such a lean 
strategy that your next roll costs $500 less in Capital if it requires 
a spend.​
 🔹 If you chose The Hustler: Your pre-launch marketing was so 
good that you get +1 to your next sales or marketing roll.​
 🔹 If you chose The Deal Maker: Your detailed planning lets 
you skip a roll the next time you negotiate pricing, ad spend, 
or a business expense. (You just get the best possible result.) 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Take your rock-solid plan and scale aggressively. → 
Go to 227 
●​ Slow down and ensure operations can keep up before 
going bigger. → Go to 228 
Planning pays off, but now it’s time to see if you can handle the 
growth.

sections.heading:
93. The Slow and Steady Approach – Solid, But
Late to the Game
sections.title: The Slow and Steady Approach – Solid, But Late to the Game
headingLines: 93. The Slow and Steady Approach – Solid, But
sections.text:
Your business plan is solid. No, it’s more than solid, it’s great. 
You’ve accounted for every possible outcome, every risk, every 
marketing angle. The problem? While you were fine-tuning 
your plan, other businesses just… launched. 
Now, you’re behind. 
Your competitors are already getting customers, testing 
strategies, and making money. Meanwhile, you’re just now 
getting started. 
No Capital gain or loss, just a slow start. 
To catch up, you need to act now. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Jump into direct outreach ASAP to start generating 
leads. → Go to 17 
●​ Refine your offer one last time before going all in. → 
Go to 19 
Overplanning won’t save you now, time to make a move.

sections.heading: 94. Analysis Paralysis – Stuck in Planning Mode
sections.title: Analysis Paralysis – Stuck in Planning Mode
headingLines: 94. Analysis Paralysis – Stuck in Planning Mode
sections.text:
You wanted a perfect plan, but now, you’re just staring at 
spreadsheets and obsessing over tiny details. 
●​ Should your logo be blue or navy blue? 
●​ Is your pricing too high or too low? 
●​ What if you launch and people don’t like it? 
Days turn into weeks, and you still haven’t made a move. 
By the time you finally snap out of it, you realize you’ve burned 
through $1,000 on software, branding tools, and courses you 
didn’t even need yet. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
Now, you have two options: 
●​ Snap out of planning mode and start selling through 
direct outreach. → Go to 17 
●​ Reassess your offer to make sure you’re actually 
solving the right problem. → Go to 19 
At some point, you just have to start. Which way are you 
going?

sections.heading: 98. The "Launch Now, Fix Later" Strategy
sections.title: The "Launch Now, Fix Later" Strategy
sections.text:
Your mentor’s advice echoes in your mind: “Stop overthinking. 
Start doing. Right now.” 
So, you take the plunge. No more tinkering, no more 
second-guessing. You throw together a basic version of your 
offer, no flashy website, no cinematic product launch, just 
something that gets into customers’ hands. 
But is this a brilliant move… or are you about to make a 
glorious mess? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → People actually love it! You land early sales, 
proving the offer has real demand. Gain $2,000 in 
Capital. → Go to 74 
●​ 8-10 → Some interest, but it's not taking off yet. You’re 
missing something crucial. No Capital gained or lost. → 
Go to 75 
●​ 7 or below → Turns out, launching before you're ready 
does come with risks, refund requests, bad reviews, and 
a customer who wants to “speak to the manager” (spoiler: 
it's you). Lose $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 76 
Your fast action could be the best decision you've ever made… or 
a total dumpster fire. Time to roll the dice.

sections.heading: 99. Word-of-Mouth Hustle – Selling on the Fly
sections.title: Word-of-Mouth Hustle – Selling on the Fly
headingLines: 99. Word-of-Mouth Hustle – Selling on the Fly
sections.text:
Your mentor basically told you to sell before you even have 
something to sell. No website? No problem. No inventory? 
Doesn’t matter. 
You start pitching everyone you know. Friends, family, old 
coworkers, even your Uber driver. One of them has to be 
interested, right? 
Some listen politely. Others avoid eye contact, like you’re about to 
pitch them an MLM scheme. But hey, if you talk to enough 
people, someone’s bound to bite. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You’re a natural! People actually buy, and your 
idea starts gaining traction. Gain $2,500 in Capital. → Go 
to 77 
●​ 8-10 → A few sales trickle in, but it’s not a game changer. 
Gain $500 in Capital. → Go to 78 
●​ 7 or below → Nobody bites, and one person even blocks 
your number. Lose 1 Resilience. → Go to 79 
Talking your way into sales is a real skill, but did you charm 
your way to success or just scare off your entire contact list?

sections.heading:
100. Stirring Up Drama – The Viral Marketing
Experiment
sections.title: Stirring Up Drama – The Viral Marketing Experiment
headingLines: 100. Stirring Up Drama – The Viral Marketing
sections.text:
Your mentor’s advice? Make noise. Get attention. It doesn’t 
matter how. 
So you go for it, a bold, slightly controversial social media 
post. Maybe you call out a bad industry trend, hype your product 
with over-the-top confidence, or just drop an outrageous meme 
and hope for the best. 
Now, you wait. Will it blow up in the best way possible or turn 
you into a cautionary tale? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Viral hit! Your post explodes, people are talking, 
and suddenly, your business has real momentum. Gain 
$3,000 in Capital. → Go to 80 
●​ 8-10 → Decent engagement, but nothing crazy. A few 
shares, some comments, but no immediate sales. Gain 
$1,000 in Capital. → Go to 81 
●​ 7 or below → Backfire. Your post gets roasted in the 
comments, and you spend the day doing damage control. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 82 
Marketing isn’t just about being seen, it’s about being seen in 
the right way. Did you strike gold or set yourself up for an 
internet disaster?

sections.heading:
101. The DM Hustle – Sliding into Potential
Customers’ Inboxes
sections.title: The DM Hustle – Sliding into Potential Customers’ Inboxes
headingLines: 101. The DM Hustle – Sliding into Potential
sections.text:
Your mentor told you to stop waiting for customers to come to 
you and start making things happen. So, you do what any 
modern entrepreneur would do… you start sending cold DMs 
like your life depends on it. 
Maybe you hit up business owners on LinkedIn, influencers 
on Instagram, or random strangers in a Facebook group. 
Either way, your fingers are flying across the keyboard as you 
craft your pitch. 
The real question is, will anyone actually respond? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Jackpot! You book calls, make sales, and start 
gaining traction. Gain $2,000 in Capital. → Go to 17 
●​ 8-10 → Some responses trickle in, but no one is handing 
over their money just yet. No Capital gained or lost. → 
Go to 19 
●​ 7 or below → One word: Blocked. You overdid it, and 
now people are calling you a scammer. Lose 1 
Resilience. → Go to 82 
Cold outreach is a powerful tool, but only if you don’t come off 
like a desperate salesperson. How did you do?

sections.heading:
102. The Warm Introduction – Leveraging Your
Network
sections.title: The Warm Introduction – Leveraging Your Network
sections.text:
Your mentor smirks and says, "Why do things the hard way 
when you can just leverage someone else's credibility?" 
That’s when it clicks, instead of cold-pitching strangers, you 
should tap into your existing network. 
You start reaching out to mutual connections, past colleagues, 
and industry contacts who might introduce you to the right 
people. If all goes well, you’ll skip the awkward cold pitch and 
go straight to real business opportunities. 
But will your contacts come through for you, or will they leave 
you on read? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Your contact hooks you up with a warm 
introduction that leads to a BIG opportunity. Gain $3,000 
in Capital. → Go to 17 
●​ 8-10 → You get a meeting, but it’s not a guaranteed win 
yet. Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 19 
●​ 7 or below → Your contact either doesn’t follow through 
or the person they introduce you to isn’t interested. Lose 
1 Resilience. → Go to 82

sections.heading:
103. The Value Exchange – Trading Skills Instead of
Spending Money
sections.title: The Value Exchange – Trading Skills Instead of Spending Money
headingLines: 103. The Value Exchange – Trading Skills Instead of
sections.text:
Your mentor leans in and says, "If you don’t have money, you 
better have value." 
So instead of spending precious Capital, you decide to barter 
your skills, services, or time to get what you need. 
Maybe you offer free marketing for a designer who’ll build 
your website, or you trade consulting hours for access to 
someone’s audience. Whatever the deal, you’re betting on your 
ability to negotiate. 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Brilliant trade! You lock in a win-win deal that 
helps your business without costing you cash. Gain 
$2,500 in Capital. → Go to 17 
●​ 8-10 → Fair exchange. You get what you need, but the 
deal isn’t life-changing. Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 
19 
●​ 7 or below → Bad deal. You overpromised and 
underdelivered, or the other person didn’t hold up their 
end. Lose 1 Resilience. → Go to 82 
Entrepreneurs who know how to trade value instead of 
spending money have a huge advantage. Did you pull off a 
smart deal, or get hustled yourself?

104. Momentum Kicks In – Turning Customers into
a Movement
sections.title: Momentum Kicks In – Turning Customers into a Movement
headingLines: 104. Momentum Kicks In – Turning Customers into
sections.text:
You did it! People are buying, and your business finally feels 
real.​
​
 
Optional Gamble – Go All In 
If you're feeling confident, you can try to stretch your systems to 
squeeze even more from the momentum! 
You can choose to take the All In Gamble.​
​
Roll 2d6 + Tech Savviness (TS): 
●​ On 10+, you hold everything together flawlessly and gain 
an extra $1,000 in Capital before reading on below.​
 
●​ On 6 or less, the surge overwhelms you → Go to 107. 
 
Your customers are excited, sharing your offer, and things are 
starting to take off. You’re finally getting a taste of success, but 
now comes the hard part, keeping it going. 
You take a moment to decide, do you push forward 
aggressively, or take a step back and stabilize first? 
Gain $3,000 in Capital. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Scale fast and go all-in on growth. → Go to 227 
●​ Stabilize your operations before expanding. → Go to 
228

sections.heading:
105. Steady Growth – Not an Explosion, But It’s
Working
sections.title: Steady Growth – Not an Explosion, But It’s Working
headingLines: 105. Steady Growth – Not an Explosion, But It’s
sections.text:
Sales are coming in, but it’s a slow trickle rather than a tidal 
wave. 
The good news? People are buying. The bad news? You’re not 
exactly rolling in cash just yet. 
You’re at a crossroads, do you stick with what’s working and 
refine it, or take a bigger risk to speed things up? 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Double down on the strategies that worked and push 
forward. → Go to 17 
●​ Tweak your messaging and offer to improve results. 
→ Go to 19

Your ads, your posts, your outreach, all met with absolute

out the window or just cry into your coffee. But quitting isn’t an 
option. You have two choices: try another marketing approach 
or go back to research and figure out what went wrong. 
Lose $1,500 in Capital. 
What do you do next?

results. → Go to 82

→ Go to 19

sections.heading: 110. A Clear Path Forward – Refining for Growth
sections.title: A Clear Path Forward – Refining for Growth
headingLines: 110. A Clear Path Forward – Refining for Growth
sections.text:
You took the feedback, refined your approach, and suddenly… 
it’s working. 
Maybe it was adjusting your pricing, tightening up your 
messaging, or simply doubling down on what worked, whatever 
the reason, you’re seeing real progress. Sales are increasing, 
customers are engaging, and you’re no longer just throwing 
ideas at the wall hoping something sticks. 
For the first time, you feel like you’re actually building 
something sustainable. 
Now comes the big decision: Do you go all in and push for 
aggressive growth, or do you stabilize your systems to make 
sure you don’t scale too fast and collapse under your own 
success? 
Gain $2,000 in Capital. 
●​ → If you want to scale aggressively and push your 
business to the next level, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to strengthen your foundations before 
expanding, go to 230.

sections.heading: 111. Slow Progress – Stuck in the Middle
sections.title: Slow Progress – Stuck in the Middle
headingLines: 111. Slow Progress – Stuck in the Middle
sections.text:
You’re making some progress, but it’s not exactly a breakthrough. 
A few more people are showing interest, maybe a couple of 
extra sales trickle in, but you’re still not where you want to be. 
You’re caught in that frustrating middle ground, too much traction 
to quit, but not enough momentum to feel like you’ve “made it.” 
The good news? You’re not losing ground.​
 The bad news? You’re not gaining much either. 
You need to decide: do you double down and push forward, or 
step back and refine your offer before scaling up? 
No Capital gain or loss. 
●​ → If you want to push forward and focus on sales 
growth, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to rework your offer to improve 
conversions, go to 230.

sections.heading:
112. Wasting Time on the Wrong Things – A Costly
Mistake
sections.title: Wasting Time on the Wrong Things – A Costly Mistake
headingLines: 112. Wasting Time on the Wrong Things – A Costly
sections.text:
You thought you were making smart improvements, but instead, 
you ended up overcomplicating everything. 
Maybe you spent too much time tweaking your website, 
changing your offer for the tenth time, or chasing shiny new 
marketing strategies that led nowhere. Whatever the case, you 
realize too late that you’ve burned through time, energy, and, 
unfortunately, money without getting any meaningful results. 
Your frustration is hitting an all-time high. You’re tempted to scrap 
everything and start over, but deep down, you know that’s not the 
move. You’ve already put in too much effort to backtrack 
completely. 
You need to regroup and make a smart next move before 
things spiral out of control. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
 
Optional Gamble – The Desperation Play 
You’re not ready to give up yet. There’s still one risky move you 
could make, a big, all-or-nothing play to recover what you 
lost. 
You can choose to take the High-Stakes Recovery Gamble. 
●​ Roll 2d6: 
○​ 10+ → A bold move pays off! You land a deal, viral 
campaign, or unexpected break. Gain $3,000 in 
Capital instead of losing $1,000. 
○​ 7-9 → Mixed results. You recover $500, but it’s not 
enough to fully bounce back. 
○​ 6 or below → Disaster. Your desperate gamble 
fails, and things get worse. Lose ALL Capital. 
Restart Act 1. 
 
If you took the gamble or chose not to, you now need to 
decide how to move forward. 
●​ → If you want to double down on a focused growth 
strategy and push forward, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to take a step back and refine your core 
offer before scaling, go to 20. 
●​ Hire staff right now to fix your problems → Go to 132

sections.heading:
113. Learning from Failure – Turning Setbacks into
Success
sections.title: Learning from Failure – Turning Setbacks into Success
headingLines: 113. Learning from Failure – Turning Setbacks into
sections.text:
The rejection stung, but instead of wallowing in self-doubt, you 
take a deep breath and analyze what went wrong. 
Maybe your messaging wasn’t clear. Maybe your pricing was off. 
Maybe you were targeting the wrong audience altogether. 
Whatever the reason, you don’t let it stop you, you adjust, pivot, 
and try again. 
And this time? Something clicks. 
People start engaging. Leads trickle in. A few sales roll through. 
It’s not an overnight explosion, but it’s proof that your idea has 
legs. 
The hardest part of entrepreneurship isn’t failing, it’s learning to 
fail forward. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
●​ → If you’re ready to double down on what’s working 
and push forward aggressively, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to refine your business foundations 
before scaling, go to 230.

sections.heading:
114. Stuck in the Middle – Slow Progress, but Still
Moving
sections.title: Stuck in the Middle – Slow Progress, but Still Moving
headingLines: 114. Stuck in the Middle – Slow Progress, but Still
sections.text:
You’ve adjusted. Tweaked. Tried new approaches. And… it’s 
helping. Sort of. 
You’re not sinking, but you’re not exactly thriving either. It’s the 
slow, frustrating middle ground, where progress is just enough 
to keep going, but not enough to break through. 
The good news? You’re learning. Every sale, every customer 
interaction, every tiny win teaches you something new. 
The bad news? If you don’t figure out how to build real 
momentum soon, you risk getting stuck in business purgatory. 
Now, it’s decision time. Do you keep grinding it out and trust 
that persistence will pay off, or do you take a bold step to shake 
things up? 
No Capital gain or loss. 
●​ → If you want to keep refining your approach and 
focus on steady progress, go to 230. 
●​ → If you’re ready to take a risk and try something big to 
break through, go to 231. 
●​  → Skip the grind and push your offer out immediately, 
unpolished, go to 121

sections.heading:
115. The Cost of Desperation – When Trying Too
Hard Backfires
sections.title: The Cost of Desperation – When Trying Too Hard Backfires
headingLines: 115. The Cost of Desperation – When Trying Too
sections.text:
You tweak. You adjust. You push harder. But instead of getting 
results, things start slipping through your fingers. 
Maybe you lowered your prices too much, chasing sales at the 
cost of profit. Maybe you jumped onto a new strategy too 
quickly, confusing your audience. Or maybe you just burned 
out, making decisions from frustration rather than logic. 
Whatever the case, it’s not working. 
The more you try to force things, the worse they get. The money 
you spent on ads, discounts, or last-minute pivots? Gone. 
Lose $2,000 in Capital. 
Now, you need to stop the bleeding before your business 
collapses. Do you slow down and reassess before making 
your next move, or do you double down and take one last 
shot at turning this around? 
●​ → If you take a step back, analyze what went wrong, and 
try to stabilize, go to 232. 
●​ → If you refuse to back down and go all-in on one last 
push, go to 233.

sections.heading:
116. The Marketing Play – Smart Spend or Costly
Lesson?
sections.title: The Marketing Play – Smart Spend or Costly Lesson?
headingLines: 116. The Marketing Play – Smart Spend or Costly
sections.text:
With cash in hand, you decide that marketing is the key to 
growth. If people don’t know about your business, they can’t buy 
from you, so it’s time to make some noise. 
You weigh your options: 
●​ Paid ads to bring in fast traffic? 
●​ Social media campaigns to build authority? 
●​ A PR stunt that could go viral, or go very, very wrong? 
Whatever you choose, one thing is clear: this money needs to 
work for you. 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Perfect Execution. Your marketing campaign is a 
huge success! Sales flood in, and your brand recognition 
skyrockets. Gain $3,000 in Capital. 
○​ Go to 227  
●​ 8-10 → Mixed Results. Some strategies pay off, others 
flop. You get some traction, but nothing groundbreaking. 
Go to 105  
●​ 7 or below → Major Misstep. Maybe your targeting was 
off, or the message didn’t resonate. Either way, you 
burned cash with little return. 
○​ Go to 112  
Marketing is a double-edged sword. Will you craft a winning 
campaign, or will your budget disappear into the abyss?

sections.heading:
117. The Product Upgrade – Worthwhile Investment
or Wasted Money?
sections.title: The Product Upgrade – Worthwhile Investment or Wasted Money?
sections.text:
Instead of throwing money into ads, you double down on your 
product. After all, if it’s not good enough to retain customers or 
generate word-of-mouth, no amount of marketing will fix that. 
You invest in improvements: 
●​ Better packaging? Check. 
●​ Enhanced features? Of course. 
●​ A high-end version for premium buyers? Why not? 
The hope? A stronger product = higher conversions, happier 
customers, and long-term growth. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Smart move! Customers love the improvements, 
and sales increase significantly. Your offer stands out, 
and you attract more high-value buyers. Gain $3,000 in 
Capital. Go to 227  
●​ 8-10 → Somewhat effective. The updates help, but not 
dramatically. Some customers appreciate the changes, 
but it’s not a game changer. Go to 105  
●​ 7 or below → Overkill. You spent too much time and 
money improving something customers didn’t really care 
about. Worse, your price increase scared off buyers. Go 
to 112  
A great product can turn customers into lifelong fans, but go 
too far, and you might end up fixing things that weren’t broken.

sections.heading:
118. Playing It Too Safe – When Caution Holds You
Back
sections.title: Playing It Too Safe – When Caution Holds You Back
headingLines: 118. Playing It Too Safe – When Caution Holds You
sections.text:
You decide to sit on most of your loan, keeping it as a financial 
cushion so you don’t run out of money too quickly. Smart, right? 
At first, it feels reassuring, like having a secret stash of cash just 
in case things go south. But here’s the thing… businesses don’t 
grow by playing defense. You need to take risks, invest, and 
actually put that money to work if you want to make more of 
it. 
Eventually, you realize that just sitting on capital isn’t a 
strategy, it’s a slow road to nowhere. You need to spend wisely 
to scale. 
●​ If you decide to invest in marketing to get more eyes 
on your offer, → Go to 116 
●​ If you focus on improving your offer before scaling 
up, → Go to 117 
Money in the bank doesn’t build a business. Time to make some 
moves.

sections.heading: 119. The Big Spend – High Risk, High Reward?
sections.title: The Big Spend – High Risk, High Reward?
headingLines: 119. The Big Spend – High Risk, High Reward?
sections.text:
You decide to go all in, betting everything on a major marketing 
push. Ads, influencers, partnerships, whatever it takes to get 
your business in front of more people fast. 
Now, you wait. Will it pay off or was this a very expensive 
lesson in what not to do? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Huge success! Your business skyrockets. → Go to 
227 
●​ 8-10 → Moderate success. Some traction, but no 
breakout moment. → Go to 228 
●​ 7 or below → Total flop. The campaign burns through 
your budget with little to show for it. → Go to 229

sections.heading:
120. Playing It Safe – Slow and Steady Wins the
Race?
sections.title: Playing It Safe – Slow and Steady Wins the Race?
headingLines: 120. Playing It Safe – Slow and Steady Wins the
sections.text:
You decide to be cautious with your spending, stretching every 
dollar and only investing in low-risk strategies. 
No massive ad campaigns, no risky partnerships, just careful, 
incremental progress. 
But will this conservative approach give your business time to 
grow, or are you just delaying the inevitable? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → You build steady momentum, laying a strong 
foundation without overspending. → Go to 227 
●​ 8-10 → Progress is slow, but at least you’re not losing 
money. → Go to 228 
●​ 7 or below → Playing it too safe means you miss key 
opportunities, your business stagnates. → Go to 229

sections.heading:
122. The Bare-Bones Hustle – Making Every Dollar
Count
sections.title: The Bare-Bones Hustle – Making Every Dollar Count
headingLines: 122. The Bare-Bones Hustle – Making Every Dollar
sections.text:
No investors. No loans. No rich uncle stepping in to fund your 
dreams. Just you, your wits, and whatever loose change you 
can scrape together from the couch cushions. 
Bootstrapping means cutting every unnecessary expense, 
running on the leanest budget possible, and grinding your way 
forward with sheer willpower. Every dollar spent has to bring in at 
least two more, and every decision must be brutally efficient. 
This is where real entrepreneurs are made, but is your lean 
strategy about to pay off or leave you living off instant ramen 
indefinitely? 
If you chose the Bootstrapper mentor, you gain 
+1 to your roll here. 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → Your discipline pays off! You stretch every dollar, 
land some early wins, and start building momentum. → 
Go to 227 
●​ 8-10 → Progress is slow, but steady. You’re making just 
enough to keep things moving. → Go to 228 
●​ 7 or below → Bootstrapping turns into barely surviving. 
You’re out of cash, out of options, and might need to start 
over. → Go to 229

sections.heading:
123. The Equity Gamble – Trading Ownership for
Funding
sections.title: The Equity Gamble – Trading Ownership for Funding
headingLines: 123. The Equity Gamble – Trading Ownership for
sections.text:
You don’t have cash, but what you do have is equity, a piece of 
your business that could be valuable… if you play your cards 
right. 
So, you start searching for the right partner, someone with 
money who believes in your vision and can help take things to 
the next level. 
But equity deals aren’t easy. Will you land a game-changing 
partner or just end up working for someone else? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You find the perfect partner, someone with 
resources and expertise. This partnership is a major win 
for your business! Go to 116. 
●​ 8-10 → You land a decent partner, but it’s not an ideal 
match. You get funding, but there are some growing 
pains. Go to 111. 
●​ 7 or below → Disaster! Your partner is a control freak, a 
flake, or just plain clueless. They’re dragging the 
business down, and now you’re stuck in a bad deal. Go to 
234.​

sections.heading:
124. The Crowdfunding Gamble – Can Strangers
Fund Your Dream?
sections.title: The Crowdfunding Gamble – Can Strangers Fund Your Dream?
sections.text:
With no investors, no loans, and no rich uncle willing to “invest” in 
your idea, you turn to the power of the internet. Crowdfunding 
could be your golden ticket, after all, people have funded 
everything from potato salad to smart refrigerators that send 
passive-aggressive reminders to buy milk. 
You put together your campaign, craft an emotional pitch, and hit 
launch. Now, it’s time to see if the internet believes in you… or if 
your campaign joins the graveyard of projects that never made it 
past their first backer. 
If you chose The Hustler as your mentor, gain +1 to your roll. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Jackpot! Your campaign goes viral, and backers 
start pouring in. You hit your goal (and then some). → Go 
to 116. 
●​ 8-10 → Some support trickles in, but it’s not a runaway 
success. You hit part of your goal, but you’ll need to 
stretch your budget. → Go to 111. 
●​ 7 or below → A total flop. No one cares, your campaign 
stagnates, and your only backer is your mom (who 
demands a refund). → Go to 236. 
Crowdfunding is high risk, high reward, but when it works, it’s like 
free money. Will your idea be the next big thing, or will the 
internet collectively ignore you?

125. The Perfect Niche – Passion, Profits, and
Potential
sections.title: The Perfect Niche – Passion, Profits, and Potential
headingLines: 125. The Perfect Niche – Passion, Profits, and
sections.text:
You did it, you found a niche that’s not only in high demand but 
actually excites you. It’s the sweet spot where passion meets 
profit, and for once, you don’t feel like you’re forcing yourself into 
a business just because someone on the internet said it was “hot 
right now.” 
People want what you have to offer, and the more you research, 
the more confident you feel. This is your lane. Now, it’s time to 
build something that fits it. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Start crafting an offer based on what you’ve learned 
and get ready to sell. → Go to 20 
●​ Play the long game, focus on building an audience 
before launching an offer. → Go to 45 
●​ Team up with someone who says they can help you 
scale faster → Go to 148 
 
A great niche is a solid foundation, but now you have to take 
action. Let’s go.

sections.heading: 126. A Decent Niche – Good, But Not Great
sections.title: A Decent Niche – Good, But Not Great
headingLines: 126. A Decent Niche – Good, But Not Great
sections.text:
You’ve landed on something viable, it’s not a runaway success, 
but it’s not a total flop either. It’s the kind of niche where you can 
make money, but you’re not waking up every morning thrilled to 
dive into it. 
Still, a decent idea executed well is far better than a brilliant idea 
that never gets off the ground. The question is, do you push 
forward with this niche, or keep looking for something better? 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Stick with it, refine your offer and start making sales. 
→ Go to 20 
●​ Take a step back and build an audience before selling 
anything. → Go to 45 
Some people make millions in the most boring niches imaginable. 
The secret? They commit and make it work.

sections.heading: 127. Niche Nightmare – You Picked a Dud
sections.title: Niche Nightmare – You Picked a Dud
headingLines: 127. Niche Nightmare – You Picked a Dud
sections.text:
You thought you struck gold. The idea made sense in your head, 
and you were sure people would love it. 
But reality? Brutal. 
No one is interested. The only engagement you’re getting is from 
your mom saying, “Looks great, sweetie!” and a few spam bots 
offering investment opportunities. Worse, you already sank 
$1,000 into domain names, prototypes, or whatever else seemed 
like a good idea at the time. 
Lose $1000 Capital.  
Time to face facts, you either need to pivot or double down and 
try to make this work. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Go back to the drawing board and rethink your offer. 
→ Go to 45 
●​ Push through, tweak the messaging, and try again. → 
Go to 20 
●​ Take random “expert advice” and pivot quickly → Go 
to 129 
Even bad ideas can succeed with the right execution… but 
maybe, just maybe, this isn’t the one.

sections.heading: 134. The Offer That Clicks – You’ve Got a Winner
sections.title: The Offer That Clicks – You’ve Got a Winner
headingLines: 134. The Offer That Clicks – You’ve Got a Winner
sections.text:
You nailed it. 
Your product or service is simple, clear, and valuable, and most 
importantly, people want it. Whether it’s a service, a digital 
product, or something physical, it solves a real problem in a way 
that makes customers say, “Shut up and take my money!” 
Now, with some early wins under your belt, you have two options: 
double down on refining and improving what works, or start 
marketing hard to scale fast. 
Gain $2,000 in Capital. 
●​ Polish the offer further to maximize conversions 
before scaling. → Go to 20 
●​ Push it out aggressively and go all-in on marketing. → 
Go to 116 
●​ Focus on tweaking small details to perfect it → Go to 
161 
●​ Go all in immediately → Go to 162 
A great offer is only half the battle, the real question is how 
fast you can get it in front of the right people.

sections.heading: 135. A Solid Start – But Needs Work
sections.title: A Solid Start – But Needs Work
headingLines: 135. A Solid Start – But Needs Work
sections.text:
It’s not bad… but it’s not great either. 
Your offer has potential, but it’s not quite hitting the mark. 
Maybe the messaging is unclear, maybe the price feels off, or 
maybe it just doesn’t excite people as much as you’d hoped. 
You get some positive feedback, a few small wins, but deep 
down, you know it could be better. 
Gain $500 in Capital. 
Now, you have a choice: 
●​ Refine and tweak your offer until it’s truly irresistible. 
→ Go to 20 
●​ Start selling anyway and improve it as you go. → Go 
to 116 
●​ Promise big results and work out how to deliver later 
→ Go to 130 
Some of the best products in the world started as rough 
drafts, the real winners are the ones who keep improving.

sections.heading:
136. Stuck in Perfectionism Hell –
Overcomplicating Everything
sections.title: Stuck in Perfectionism Hell – Overcomplicating Everything
sections.text:
You wanted it to be perfect. 
Every little detail had to be just right. The branding? Flawless. 
The messaging? Refined to a science. The offer? A masterpiece 
of marketing and psychology. 
…At least, that was the plan. 
The problem? You never actually launched. 
Instead of getting your offer in front of real customers, you spent 
weeks (or months) obsessing over tweaks that no one but you 
would ever notice. And in the process, you burned through time 
and resources with nothing to show for it. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
Now, you have to face reality: 
●​ Scrap the perfectionism, launch what you have, and 
start selling NOW. → Go to 116 
●​ Take a step back and simplify everything into 
something clear and actionable. → Go to 111 
●​ Scrap everything to chase a shiny new idea → Go to 
131 
Perfectionism is the enemy of progress, real businesses are 
built in the marketplace, not in your head.

sections.heading:
138. Slow But Steady – Building Relationships Over
Time
sections.title: Slow But Steady – Building Relationships Over Time
headingLines: 138. Slow But Steady – Building Relationships Over
sections.text:
Networking is weird. Sometimes you meet exactly the right 
person at the right time, and sometimes, you just have a bunch 
of awkward small talk and vague promises to “collaborate 
someday.” 
This time, it’s the latter. 
You’ve definitely met some interesting people, maybe even 
future allies, but no one is throwing money at you just yet. Still, 
you’re planting seeds, and if you keep nurturing these 
connections, something might come of it later. 
For now, though, what do you want to do? 
●​ Double down on your business and focus on 
marketing your offer, → Go to 116. 
●​ Pivot and refine your offer further before pushing 
ahead, → Go to 20. 
●​ Just pitch everyone you meet with a rehearsed 
messaged playing the numbers game → Go to 128

sections.heading:
139. Networking Nightmare – Awkward, Expensive,
and Useless
sections.title: Networking Nightmare – Awkward, Expensive, and Useless
sections.text:
Some people thrive in networking environments. You are not one 
of those people. 
Maybe you spent way too much on an event that was just a 
bunch of “gurus” selling courses. Maybe you tried to impress a 
big shot and completely fumbled the conversation. Or maybe 
no one even acknowledged your existence, just you, standing 
awkwardly, clutching a half-empty cup of bad coffee. 
Either way, this was a disaster. 
You lose $1,000 in Capital (because travel, tickets, and 
overpriced cocktails add up), and you leave with nothing but 
regret and a lanyard you’ll never wear again. 
●​ If you decide to forget networking and go all-in on 
selling your offer, → Go to 116. 
●​ If you take this as a learning experience and work on 
improving your business first, → Go to 20. 
●​ Take the lesson in stride and refocus your energy 
online instead → Go to 163

sections.heading:
140. A Marketing Blitz – More Eyes, More Sales, or
More Money Burned?
sections.title: A Marketing Blitz – More Eyes, More Sales, or More Money Burned?
headingLines: 140. A Marketing Blitz – More Eyes, More Sales, or
sections.text:
You decide to go all-in on marketing. Maybe it’s paid ads, 
influencer shoutouts, or some wild PR stunt that totally won’t 
backfire. The goal? Get as many people as possible to see 
your offer, fast. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → The gamble pays off. The campaign works, 
customers start rolling in, and your business gets a real 
boost. → Go to 116. 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed results. Some sales come in, but it’s not a 
game changer. → Go to 111. 
●​ 7 or below → Marketing fail. You burn through cash with 
little to show for it. Lose $2,000 in Capital. → Go to 236. 
Marketing can be a gold mine or a money pit, it all depends on 
the execution.

sections.heading: 141. Refining Your Offer – Making It Irresistible
sections.title: Refining Your Offer – Making It Irresistible
headingLines: 141. Refining Your Offer – Making It Irresistible
sections.text:
Instead of rushing to market, you take a step back. Maybe your 
product is solid, but the messaging needs work. Maybe the 
service is valuable, but the delivery could be smoother. 
You spend time tweaking, improving, and testing. The result? A 
stronger, clearer, and more compelling offer. 
Now, when you pitch it, people get it, and that means more sales. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
Now it’s time to put your work to the test. What’s your next move? 
●​ Time to launch, push your marketing and get this in 
front of customers. → Go to 116 
●​ Start selling organically, test the waters before going 
all in. → Go to 46 
●​ Try to make a bold, flashy PR stunt → Go to 133

sections.heading:
143: The Hustle to Pay Them Back – No More
Owing Anyone
sections.title: The Hustle to Pay Them Back – No More Owing Anyone
headingLines: 143: The Hustle to Pay Them Back – No More
sections.text:
The best way to get someone off your back? Pay them back, 
fast. 
You double down on sales, cut expenses, and work 
ridiculous hours. Maybe you’re burning the midnight oil, pulling 
off last-minute deals, or convincing people they need your 
product right now. 
Your investor (or concerned family member) wants their money 
back, and you deliver, but at what cost? 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → You grind hard, land some big wins, and pay them 
back in record time. No more pressure, and your business 
is still intact. Gain $3,000 in Capital. → Go to 240 
●​ 8-10 → You manage to pay them back, but it comes at a 
price, burnout, stress, or rushing a few things. No Capital 
gain or loss, but you’re exhausted. → Go to 241 
●​ 7 or below → You push too hard, make reckless 
decisions, and things spiral. Instead of getting ahead, you 
end up in a worse position than before. Lose $2,000 in 
Capital. → Go to 242

sections.heading:
144. Negotiation Tactics – Can You Change the
Deal?
sections.title: Negotiation Tactics – Can You Change the Deal?
headingLines: 144. Negotiation Tactics – Can You Change the
sections.text:
The pressure is on, and you’re not about to let a bad deal sink 
your business. Time to use your charm, logic, or sheer 
desperation to renegotiate better terms. 
Maybe you offer a revenue-sharing agreement instead of an 
upfront repayment, push for more flexible deadlines, or just 
convince them that they should really believe in your long-term 
vision. 
But will they go for it? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Your negotiation skills are on point. They agree to 
better terms, easing the pressure and letting you focus 
on growing. Gain $1,500 in Capital. → Go to 243 
●​ 8-10 → It’s a mixed result. You get some breathing 
room, but they still expect regular updates and payments. 
No Capital gain or loss. → Go to 244 
●​ 7 or below → Disaster. Your attempt backfires 
spectacularly, and now they want their money back 
immediately, with interest. Lose $2,000 in Capital. → 
Go to 245

sections.heading: 145. Sticking to the Plan – Hoping for Patience
sections.title: Sticking to the Plan – Hoping for Patience
headingLines: 145. Sticking to the Plan – Hoping for Patience
sections.text:
You decide to stick to your original plan and trust that your 
investor (aka your friend, uncle, or overly enthusiastic mom) will 
stay patient while you work on making the business a success. 
You stay focused, use the money wisely, and avoid any 
unnecessary stress… for now. 
But will they stay patient or start nagging you for updates 
every five minutes? 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → They’re totally chill. They trust you, stay 
hands-off, and even offer more support if needed. Gain 
$1,500 in Capital. → Go to 246 
●​ 8-10 → They check in occasionally, but nothing too 
stressful. As long as they see progress, they’re fine… for 
now. No Capital gain or loss. → Go to 247 
●​ 7 or below → Big mistake. They start pressuring you 
non-stop, demanding updates, asking about profits, and 
even hinting at wanting their money back soon. Lose 
$2,000 in Capital. → Go to 248

sections.heading:
146. Hardcore Bootstrapping – Making Every Dollar
Count
sections.title: Hardcore Bootstrapping – Making Every Dollar Count
sections.text:
No money? No problem. 
You decide to fully embrace the bootstrapper lifestyle, cutting 
every expense that isn’t absolutely necessary. Forget fancy 
software, paid ads, or even that overpriced oat milk latte, you’re in 
full grind mode now. 
If you chose The Bootstrapper as your mentor earlier, they step 
in to teach you some creative ways to stretch your resources 
and turn pennies into profit. Gain +1 to this roll. 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE) (+1 if mentored by The 
Bootstrapper): 
●​ 11+ → You make it work. Hustling hard, keeping costs 
low, and reinvesting wisely pays off. Your business starts 
gaining traction. → Go to 113  
●​ 8-10 → It’s a slow grind. You keep the business running 
but progress is slow. At least you’re not losing money. → 
Go to 114 
●​ 7 or below → Reality hits hard. Starving for success 
sounds cool, until you realize you’re actually starving. 
Your lack of funding stalls progress, and you struggle to 
grow. → Go to 115

sections.heading:
147. The Search for an Investor – Finding the Right
Backer
sections.title: The Search for an Investor – Finding the Right Backer
headingLines: 147. The Search for an Investor – Finding the Right
sections.text:
You need money, and you’re not giving up. If friends and family 
won’t invest, then it’s time to look elsewhere. 
That means networking, pitching, and convincing someone with 
deep pockets that you and your business are worth betting on. 
But investors aren’t just handing out cash, you’ll need to 
impress them. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You land an investor who believes in your vision. 
They offer you a fair deal, and suddenly, your business 
has fuel to grow. → Go to 31 
●​ 8-10 → You get a conditional offer, but it comes with 
strings attached. Maybe the investor wants too much 
control, maybe the deal has harsh terms, or maybe they’re 
just hard to work with. Do you accept? 
○​ Accept the deal and take the risk. → Go to 38 . 
○​ Decline and keep searching. → Go to 146  
●​ 7 or below → No luck. Investors either ghost you, reject 
you, or laugh you out of the room. You wasted time and 
got nowhere. → Go to 39

sections.heading: 148. When the Shortcut Costs You
sections.title: When the Shortcut Costs You
sections.text:
It seemed like the fastest way out: join forces with someone who 
promised quick wins.​
 
At first, it looked like progress, but soon you’re cleaning up their 
mess, footing the bills, and realizing they weren’t ready to pull 
their weight. 
Lose $600 in Capital. 
→ Go to 240.

sections.heading:
149. Refining the Winning Strategy – Tweaking for
Maximum Impact
sections.title: Refining the Winning Strategy – Tweaking for Maximum Impact
headingLines: 149. Refining the Winning Strategy – Tweaking for
sections.text:
You’ve struck gold, or at least some kind of shiny metal, with 
this strategy, and now it’s time to refine it. 
Maybe it’s tightening up your messaging, streamlining your 
process, or cutting out the fluff that doesn’t actually matter. 
Either way, you know that small tweaks can make a big 
difference. 
Rather than blindly scaling, you decide to sharpen your offer 
and make sure it’s as strong as possible before going all in. 
Smart move. Now, where do you focus? 
●​ Double down on refining your offer and making it 
stronger. → Go to 20.

sections.heading: 150. Full Speed Ahead – Selling Like a Pro
sections.title: Full Speed Ahead – Selling Like a Pro
headingLines: 150. Full Speed Ahead – Selling Like a Pro
sections.text:
You’ve got the strategy, you’ve got the confidence, and now it’s 
time to sell like your life depends on it (because, financially, it 
kind of does). 
No more hesitation. No more second-guessing. It’s time to hit the 
gas and start pushing your offer out into the world with everything 
you’ve got. 
Maybe that means running ads, cold emailing, or turning your 
social media into a non-stop sales machine, whatever it takes 
to get paying customers fast. 
●​ You go all in on marketing and selling as aggressively 
as possible. → Go to 227.

sections.heading: 151. Testing the Waters – Cautious but Calculated
sections.title: Testing the Waters – Cautious but Calculated
headingLines: 151. Testing the Waters – Cautious but Calculated
sections.text:
You’ve learned your lesson, you’re not about to go all in blindly 
and risk everything again. 
Instead, you take a smarter, measured approach. You test your 
strategy, analyze results, and make small adjustments before 
going all out. 
●​ Maybe you launch a small-scale marketing campaign 
instead of spending everything upfront. 
●​ Maybe you sell to a test group first, getting feedback 
before expanding. 
●​ Maybe you just want one more sign from the universe 
before committing fully. 
Either way, you’re playing it safe, but you’re still moving forward. 
●​ You carefully refine your approach and only scale up 
when you see proof that it works. → Go to 228.

sections.heading: 152: Refining the Formula – Small Wins Add Up
sections.title: Refining the Formula – Small Wins Add Up
headingLines: 152: Refining the Formula – Small Wins Add Up
sections.text:
You take what’s working and double down. Maybe you fine-tune 
your messaging, tweak your pricing, or just get better at delivering 
what you promised. 
At first, it’s slow. A few sales here, some engagement there. But 
over time, those small improvements start adding up. Suddenly, 
you’re not just trying, you’re actually making real progress. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
What’s next? 
●​ Push for aggressive growth now that you’ve got some 
traction. → Go to 227 
●​ Keep refining your offer to maximize results before 
scaling. → Go to 20 
●​ Keep testing and adjusting, you’re still figuring things 
out. → Go to 111 
The right move isn’t always about going bigger, it’s about getting 
better.

sections.heading:
153: Rethinking the Strategy – Time for a New
Approach
sections.title: Rethinking the Strategy – Time for a New Approach
headingLines: 153: Rethinking the Strategy – Time for a New
sections.text:
Something’s off. No matter how much you tweak and test, this 
strategy just isn’t delivering the results you need. Maybe the 
market isn’t responding, maybe the competition is too strong, or 
maybe you’re just plain tired of forcing something that doesn’t feel 
right. 
Instead of banging your head against the wall, you decide it’s 
time for a fresh perspective. 
What’s next? 
●​ Pivot your offer, adjust what you’re selling to better 
match demand. → Go to 20 
●​ Shift your marketing strategy and try reaching a 
different audience. → Go to 116 
●​ Take a step back, review your data, and analyze 
what’s not working. → Go to 111 
Sometimes, success isn’t about pushing harder, it’s about 
knowing when to change direction.

sections.heading: 154: Hitting Pause – Taking a Step Back to Regroup
sections.title: Hitting Pause – Taking a Step Back to Regroup
headingLines: 154: Hitting Pause – Taking a Step Back to Regroup
sections.text:
Burnout is real. You’ve been grinding non-stop, testing strategies, 
making adjustments, and pushing forward… but something feels 
off. Instead of running yourself into the ground, you decide to take 
a step back, breathe, and regroup. 
It’s not quitting, it’s strategizing. 
●​ If you have The Bootstrapper as your mentor, they 
remind you that hustling smart is better than hustling 
hard. Gain $500 in Capital for making a calculated 
decision. 
After a short reset, what’s your next move? 
●​ Re-evaluate your approach and refine your current 
strategy. → Go to 111 
●​ Explore a completely new angle to market your offer. 
→ Go to 116 
●​ Reignite your motivation and push forward with fresh 
energy. → Go to 20 
Even the best entrepreneurs know when to step back and reset, 
it’s how you come back stronger.

sections.heading:
155. Pivot Fast – Cut Your Losses and Find a Real
Strategy
sections.title: Pivot Fast – Cut Your Losses and Find a Real Strategy
headingLines: 155. Pivot Fast – Cut Your Losses and Find a Real
sections.text:
Enough is enough. You’re done chasing fake gurus and magic 
formulas. If you’re going to make this work, it’ll be on your own 
terms. 
You take a step back, rethink your approach, and start focusing 
on real business fundamentals. No more get-rich-quick nonsense, 
just solid strategy and execution. 
Now, it’s time to take action. 
What’s your next move?

sections.heading:
156. The Dark Side of Business – Selling a Bad
Course
sections.title: The Dark Side of Business – Selling a Bad Course
headingLines: 156. The Dark Side of Business – Selling a Bad
sections.text:
You made the choice. You resold the guru’s course, hoping to 
make back your money. 
And it worked… for about five minutes. 
Then the messages started rolling in. 
Your buyer has questions you can’t answer, expectations you 
can’t meet, and frustration that quickly turns into public 
outrage. Word spreads fast, and suddenly, you’re being blasted 
in forums, social media groups, and even your own inbox. 
People are calling you a scammer. Your credibility is in 
shambles. And the worst part? You didn’t even make that much 
money. 
Lose $2,000 in Capital (including refunds, chargebacks, and 
damage control).​
 Lose 1 Networking (NE) – Your reputation takes a hit, 
making it harder to build trust. 
You can’t build long-term success on shady deals. 
●​ You realize your mistake and commit to learning the 
right way. → Go to 157

sections.heading: 157. Back to Basics – The Power of Free Resources
sections.title: Back to Basics – The Power of Free Resources
headingLines: 157. Back to Basics – The Power of Free Resources
sections.text:
Burned by the guru, out a chunk of cash, and determined not to 
get fooled again, you do what you should have done from the 
start, dig into free, high-quality resources. 
You binge marketing blogs, watch YouTube breakdowns, listen to 
business podcasts, and even go through actual case studies 
from people who built real businesses. 
And guess what? It actually helps. 
You start piecing together a real strategy, not based on hype, 
but on actual principles that work. It takes longer, but it builds 
real skills instead of just filling your head with motivational 
nonsense. 
Gain 1 Creativity (CR) – You learn how to think for yourself 
instead of blindly following advice. 
Now, it’s time to refine your offer and apply what you’ve 
learned. 
→ Go to 20

leverage this success.

to 227

to 228

sections.text:

It’s frustrating, but at least you know you’re on the right path. 
Now, do you double down and refine your approach further, 
or do you take a step back and look for a bigger opportunity? 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
●​ Refine your approach even more and try to push 
through. → Go to 20 
●​ Look for a completely fresh strategy instead. → Go to 
45

sections.heading: 160. The Wrong Move – A Pivot Gone Bad
sections.title: The Wrong Move – A Pivot Gone Bad
headingLines: 160. The Wrong Move – A Pivot Gone Bad
sections.text:
You took a leap… and landed flat on your face. 
Maybe you changed too much, lost the trust of your audience, or 
just confused the heck out of everyone. Whatever the reason, this 
pivot didn’t just stall your progress, it set you back. 
Lose $1,500 in Capital. 
Now, you’re scrambling to recover. The only way forward? Go 
back to the basics and refine your offer. 
→ Go to 113 
A smart pivot can change everything. A bad one? Well… at least 
you learned what not to do.

sections.heading: 164. The Service Boom – Clients, Cash, and Chaos
sections.title: The Service Boom – Clients, Cash, and Chaos
headingLines: 164. The Service Boom – Clients, Cash, and Chaos
sections.text:
Boom. You hit the ground running. 
Maybe it was your pitch, maybe it was dumb luck, or maybe you 
were just that good, but clients are signing up, and your service 
business is making real money. 
Gain $3,000 in Capital. 
Now, what’s next? 
●​ Use this momentum to refine your offer and increase 
prices. → Go to 20 
●​ Expand your marketing efforts to attract even more 
clients. → Go to 227 
 
Success is great, but smart entrepreneurs don’t just chase more 
work, they figure out how to make more while doing less.

sections.heading: 165. The Service Grind – Slow, but Steady Progress
sections.title: The Service Grind – Slow, but Steady Progress
headingLines: 165. The Service Grind – Slow, but Steady Progress
sections.text:
You’re getting clients, but it’s not the flood of business you 
imagined. 
Maybe your pricing isn’t quite right, maybe you’re struggling to 
stand out, or maybe you just need more time. Either way, you’re 
making progress, it’s just slower than you’d like. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
Now, how do you speed things up? 
●​ Double down on outreach to land bigger clients. → Go 
to 137 
●​ Refine your offer to make it more irresistible. → Go to 
20 
●​ Focus on expanding your circle and meet as many 
new people as possible. → Go to 143​
 
It’s not about how fast you start, it’s about how you scale. Keep 
tweaking, keep testing, and keep moving forward.

sections.heading: 166. The Service Struggle – When No One’s Buying
sections.title: The Service Struggle – When No One’s Buying
headingLines: 166. The Service Struggle – When No One’s Buying
sections.text:
Crickets. Nothing. Your inbox is as empty as your wallet. 
You thought selling a service would be easy, just offer what you’re 
good at, and people will pay, right? Turns out, getting clients is its 
own skill, and you haven’t quite cracked the code yet. 
Lose $1,500 in Capital. 
Now, you’re stuck. Do you pivot, push harder, or rethink your 
entire approach? 
●​ Go back to the drawing board and refine your 
positioning. → Go to 20 
●​ Try networking and leveraging referrals to get your 
first few clients. → Go to 138 
Selling is an art, and right now, you’re finger-painting. Time to 
level up.

167: The Slow Burn Pays Off – Monetizing Your
Audience
sections.title: The Slow Burn Pays Off – Monetizing Your Audience
headingLines: 167: The Slow Burn Pays Off – Monetizing Your
sections.text:
It took time, consistency, and maybe a little bit of blind faith, but 
your audience is finally growing. People recognize you. They 
engage with your content. Some even ask when you’re launching 
a product. 
Now comes the big decision: Do you start selling now or keep 
growing before making your move? 
Gain $2,000 in Capital from early sponsorships, brand deals, or 
pre-sales. 
But now, you have a decision to make: 
●​ Monetize now and start selling to your audience. → 
Go to 227 
●​ Keep growing your audience before selling anything. 
→ Go to 235 
An audience is powerful, but only if you know how to use it.

sections.heading:
168. Slow and Steady – Building an Audience Takes
Time
sections.title: Slow and Steady – Building an Audience Takes Time
headingLines: 168. Slow and Steady – Building an Audience Takes
sections.text:
You’re getting some traction, but it’s slow. 
People are engaging with your content, but the growth feels like 
watching paint dry. No overnight success stories here, just the 
grind of posting, tweaking, and hoping the algorithm decides to 
bless you. 
Still, at least some people are paying attention. The question 
is, how do you turn this into actual momentum? 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Double down on consistency and keep pushing 
forward. → Go to 235 
●​ Refine your content strategy and try again. → Go to 
237 
Growing an audience isn’t flashy, it’s about who sticks with it 
the longest. Are you in, or are you out?

sections.heading: 169. Content Flop – When Nobody Cares
sections.title: Content Flop – When Nobody Cares
sections.text:
Your content… isn’t hitting. 
Maybe you picked the wrong platform, maybe your message isn’t 
clear, or maybe people just aren’t that into your deep dive on 
the economics of artisanal soap-making. Whatever the case, 
it’s not working. 
Worse, you’ve spent money on tools, ads, and a “course” 
from a so-called content expert who just reposts motivational 
quotes. And now? You’re down $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Pivot, time to refine your message and try a new 
angle. → Go to 237 
●​ Abandon content and focus on direct sales instead. → 
Go to 20 
Not everyone is built for content creation, but failing at one 
strategy doesn’t mean you’re out of the game. Adapt or fade 
into obscurity.

You’re not just getting attention, you’re making money.​
 Gain $4,000 in Capital.

attention? 
●​ Double down and ride the momentum with more 
viral-style content → Go to 173

long-term brand → Go to 235 
●​ Chase a viral stunt → Go to 198 
Sometimes the worst thing about going viral… is figuring out what 
to do after it happens.

headingLines: 171. A Bit of Buzz – But No Breakout
sections.text:
You went for viral, and hey, something kinda worked. 
You got some likes, a few shares, and one guy commented, 
“This.”  
It’s not crickets, but it’s not takeoff, either. 
The attention gives you a small boost in confidence and a few 
curious visitors. But now, you need to decide what to do next. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
●​ Tweak your content and keep chasing that viral 
breakthrough. → Go to 173 
●​ Shift your focus toward building something more stable. → 
Go to 235 
Going viral is fun… but building a business that lasts? That’s 
where the real magic happens.

sections.heading: 172. Viral Flop – The Internet Shrugs
sections.title: Viral Flop – The Internet Shrugs
sections.text:
You tried to go viral. You gave it everything, bold hook, spicy take, 
snappy caption.​
 And the internet responded with… total silence. 
No views. No likes. Not even a pity share from your cousin. 
Was it the algorithm? The timing? Or maybe people just weren’t 
ready for your “Entrepreneurial Squat Challenge”? 
Whatever it was, the viral dream dies here. 
Lose $1,500 in Capital.​
 (Time spent, tools bought, maybe even a little paid traffic that 
went nowhere.) 
Now what? 
●​ Go back to refining your core offer before trying again. → 
Go to 20​
 
Sometimes you’ve got to crash and burn before you figure out 
what really works.

sections.heading: 173. Turning a Scam into Stardom
sections.title: Turning a Scam into Stardom
sections.text:
Your confession about getting scammed spreads faster than free 
pizza at a startup convention. Instead of mockery, people admire 
your brutal honesty. 
Your inbox floods with messages thanking you for saving others 
from the same costly mistake. A well-known podcaster invites you 
onto her show, calling you "the entrepreneur brave enough to 
speak truth to gurus." Overnight, your embarrassing setback 
becomes your biggest asset, proving that vulnerability can build 
serious credibility. 
Soon, coaching requests, collaboration offers, and even 
sponsorship deals roll in. Your mentor messages: “I knew honesty 
would pay off. Now, use this momentum wisely.” 
Gain $3,000 in Capital from coaching sessions, sponsorships, 
and partnerships. 
With influence and cash in hand, what's your next step? 
●​ Quickly launch a paid coaching program to capitalize on 
demand. → Go to 194 
●​ Turn your credibility into a long-term content-based 
business. → Go to 196 
●​ Create and market a product designed to protect others 
from guru scams. → Go to 197

sections.heading: 174. A Whisper, Not a Shout
sections.title: A Whisper, Not a Shout
sections.text:
You bravely share your guru-course disaster online, hoping 
authenticity might spark interest. It gets attention, but nothing 
groundbreaking. Some comments applaud your honesty, others 
share their similar mistakes, but it doesn't blow up as you'd 
hoped. 
Still, not all is lost. A few people message you privately, genuinely 
thankful for your transparency. One even asks if you offer 
consultations. It's not a flood of opportunities, but it's something, 
proof your honesty resonates, even if quietly. 
Your mentor reassures you: "Authority builds slowly. Keep sharing 
real value consistently, and it'll pay off eventually." 
Gain $1,000 in Capital from early coaching sessions or small 
partnership deals. 
With modest momentum starting to build, what’s your next move? 
●​ Offer personalized coaching sessions immediately to 
maximize your small but eager audience. → Go to 194 
●​ Slowly build a content-based brand, betting on steady 
growth. → Go to 196 
●​ Develop a niche product specifically helping others avoid 
guru scams, using your story as the foundation. → Go to 
197

sections.heading: 175. Backfire – Lost in Complaints
sections.title: Backfire – Lost in Complaints
sections.text:
You thought honesty would build trust, so you openly shared your 
guru-course disaster. Instead of empathy, your posts trigger 
skepticism and criticism. Comments accuse you of playing the 
victim or whining about your own mistakes. Even your mentor 
gently cautions, “There’s a thin line between authenticity and 
oversharing.” 
Discouraged, you realize you've inadvertently damaged your 
credibility. A couple of potential clients back away, concerned 
you're not experienced enough to guide them. The setback 
stings, and you're reminded that not every lesson needs public 
airing. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital (lost opportunities and credibility). 
Feeling the burn of this backlash, what's your next step? 
●​ Immediately offer targeted coaching sessions to rebuild 
trust quietly. → Go to 194 
●​ Take a step back and focus on building authority through 
consistent, value-driven content. → Go to 196 
●​ Create a practical product specifically designed to protect 
others from guru scams, turning your mistake into 
actionable solutions. → Go to 197

sections.heading: 176. Partnership Perfection – Accelerating Growth
sections.title: Partnership Perfection – Accelerating Growth
sections.text:
The deal couldn't have gone better. Your new partner delivers 
exactly what you needed: significant funding, powerful 
connections, and a network that instantly boosts your visibility. 
Almost overnight, sales surge, your audience grows rapidly, and 
opportunities flood your inbox. 
Your mentor sends a simple but satisfying message: “Now that’s 
how you leverage partnerships. Nice work!” 
With your business thriving, you know your next step is critical. 
You have momentum, capital, and credibility, everything you’ve 
dreamed of. But how you manage growth from here will 
determine if this partnership continues to pay off or fizzles under 
pressure. 
Gain $4,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next strategic move? 
●​ Aggressively scale your business to maximize this 
momentum. → Go to 227 
●​ Take time to stabilize operations before expanding further. 
→ Go to 228 
●​ Chase a new strategy everyone is talking about. → Go to 
199

sections.heading: 177. A Deal with Strings Attached
sections.title: A Deal with Strings Attached
sections.text:
The partnership seemed promising, but reality quickly sets in. 
Sure, you gained useful resources and some much-needed 
capital, but your partner’s growing demands start taking their toll. 
You’re spending more time fulfilling their conditions than focusing 
on your vision. 
Your mentor advises caution: “Not every partnership is perfect. 
Decide now whether to take back control or find ways to leverage 
this situation more wisely.” 
You realize this imperfect deal still provides benefits, you have 
extra capital and newfound exposure, but at what cost? You must 
act quickly before this situation derails your business entirely. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
What's your next move? 
●​ Reassert control and negotiate firmly to improve 
partnership terms. → Go to 144 
●​ Accept the current terms, leveraging this deal as a 
stepping stone while quietly planning your exit. → Go to 
152 
●​ Cut your losses immediately, end the partnership, and 
pivot quickly. → Go to 155​

sections.heading:
178. Partnership Nightmare – Burning Bridges and
Cash
sections.title: Partnership Nightmare – Burning Bridges and Cash
sections.text:
The partnership you eagerly embraced turns sour almost 
immediately. Your supposed “ally” promised resources but 
delivered nothing, leaving you buried in obligations, unpaid 
invoices, and frustration. Your mentor’s gentle advice stings: “You 
trusted too quickly. Partnerships only work when both sides 
deliver.” 
You realize you've lost valuable time and money, your momentum 
grinding to a halt. You’ll need to move swiftly to recover, rebuild, 
and regain lost confidence. The experience hurts, but if 
entrepreneurship taught you anything, it's how to adapt quickly. 
Lose $2,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next critical move? 
●​ Pivot immediately, launch a simple service-based offer, 
and start recovering lost funds quickly. → Go to 44 
●​ Take a strategic pause, regroup, and carefully craft a new 
plan to relaunch stronger. → Go to 154 
●​ Try turning this painful failure into powerful content to 
regain credibility and authority. → Go to 47​

sections.title: Master Negotiator – Turning a Loss into Leverage
headingLines: 179. Master Negotiator – Turning a Loss into
sections.text:
Your tactical skills pay off brilliantly. Calmly but assertively, you 
reach out to the guru's support team and negotiate skillfully. After 
some back-and-forth, they offer a partial refund and even 
sweeten the deal by giving you complimentary access to another 
one of their high-value programs. 
You’ve effectively turned a frustrating loss into a powerful new 
resource and a much-needed boost in capital. 
Gain $2,500 in Capital. 
Now, armed with extra cash and fresh insights, what’s your next 
strategic move? 
●​ Aggressively reinvest your newfound capital into 
marketing your existing business offer. → Go to 116 
●​ Carefully refine your current offer, ensuring everything is 
solid before scaling further. → Go to 141 
●​ Pivot quickly and launch a fresh offer inspired by the new 
bonus materials. → Go to 158

sections.heading: 180. Partial Win – Softening the Blow
sections.title: Partial Win – Softening the Blow
sections.text:
Your negotiation skills are solid enough to make an impact, but 
the guru’s team won’t fully budge. Still, persistence earns you a 
modest victory. They reluctantly agree to provide a small refund 
and some bonus materials, hoping it’s enough to keep you quiet. 
It's not exactly the outcome you wanted, but it eases your loss 
slightly. At least you’ve clawed something back from what initially 
felt like a total defeat. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
With a bit of money recovered and new material in hand, what’s 
your next move? 
●​ Use the small cash injection to launch a targeted 
marketing campaign, aiming for quick sales to rebuild 
momentum. → Go to 140 
●​ Take time to carefully study the bonus materials, refining 
your offer before launching it again. → Go to 152 
●​ Pivot entirely, crafting a fresh, low-risk product designed 
specifically from insights gained through this partial 
victory. → Go to 158

sections.heading:
181. Negotiation Nightmare – Shut Down and Shut
Out
sections.title: Negotiation Nightmare – Shut Down and Shut Out
headingLines: 181. Negotiation Nightmare – Shut Down and Shut
sections.text:
You make your best attempt at negotiation, clearly outlining why 
you deserve at least a partial refund. Unfortunately, the guru’s 
team quickly shuts you down. They cite "strict no-refund policies," 
leaving no room for compromise. 
Frustrated, you realize your time spent chasing this refund has 
only drained your energy and damaged your confidence. Now 
you're even further behind, feeling burned and disillusioned. 
Lose $500 in Capital (from wasted time and effort). 
With fewer resources and morale shaken, you need a quick 
strategy to bounce back: 
●​ Immediately launch a simple, service-based offer to 
rebuild momentum and confidence quickly. → Go to 44 
●​ Regroup carefully, spending some quiet time planning a 
stronger relaunch of your original idea. → Go to 154 
●​ Create transparent content about this painful experience 
to regain some credibility and authority through honesty. 
→ Go to 47

sections.heading:
182. Refining Your Business – Turning Wisdom into
Action
sections.title: Refining Your Business – Turning Wisdom into Action
headingLines: 182. Refining Your Business – Turning Wisdom into
sections.text:
The nugget you discovered buried deep in that overpriced course 
is genuinely useful. Eager to squeeze value from your expensive 
mistake, you quickly integrate this powerful tactic into your 
business approach. 
Almost immediately, your confidence grows. You tighten your 
sales pitch, adjust pricing, and streamline your marketing 
message, each decision shaped by your newfound tactical 
insight. 
Early feedback from customers confirms you're on the right track. 
Momentum returns, cautiously optimistic but unmistakably 
positive. Maybe the money wasn’t completely wasted after all. 
Your Tactics (TA) have permanently increased by +1. 
What's your next strategic move? 
●​ Use this refined strategy to immediately launch an 
aggressive marketing campaign. → Go to 140 
●​ Take time to perfect your offer, aiming for long-term, 
sustainable growth. → Go to 141 
●​ Test your improved approach carefully before scaling, 
minimizing further risk. → Go to 151​

sections.heading: 183. Quick Cash Grab – Racing Against Regret
sections.title: Quick Cash Grab – Racing Against Regret
headingLines: 183. Quick Cash Grab – Racing Against Regret
sections.text:
With nearly five grand down the drain, your only goal is 
immediate recovery. The nugget of wisdom you found is your 
lifeline. You rapidly implement this new tactic, hoping for quick 
results. 
You launch a targeted promotion, adjust your pricing strategy, and 
aggressively market your updated offer. It’s messy, rushed, and 
stressful, but it works. Sales trickle in slowly, bringing relief and 
some desperately needed confidence. 
Your improved tactics help, but you're still far from breaking even. 
This is just the start, but it proves your golden nugget might save 
your investment after all. 
Your Tactics (TA) have permanently increased by +1. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
With some immediate results, what's your next move? 
●​ Keep doubling down aggressively, increasing ad spend to 
scale fast. → Go to 116 
●​ Slow down to carefully optimize your funnel, maximizing 
long-term returns. → Go to 141 
●​ Quickly pivot into a related niche using your newfound 
insights. → Go to 158​
